sentences.en: This is the 99% Invisible Breakdown of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《99%隐形》宪法解析系列。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: And I'm Elizabeth Jo.
sentences.zh: 我是伊丽莎白·乔。

sentences.en: Today, we are finishing up our discussion of Article 2, which establishes the executive branch of the federal government.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将结束对第二条的讨论，该条款确立了联邦政府的行政部门。

sentences.en: Our special guest for this episode is Dr. Tom Frieden, who served as director of the Center for Disease Control and Prevention under President Obama from 2009 to 2017.
sentences.zh: 本期节目的特邀嘉宾是汤姆·弗里登博士，他曾在奥巴马总统任内（2009年至2017年）担任美国疾病控制与预防中心主任。

sentences.en: We brought him on to talk about the experience of being a highly trained expert in an inherently political institution.
sentences.zh: 我们请他来谈谈在一个本质上政治化的机构中，作为一名训练有素的专家是种什么样的体验。

sentences.en: That was once considered to be about as apolitical as you can get, but not so much anymore.
sentences.zh: 那个机构曾经被认为是非常超脱政治的，但现在已经大不如前了。

sentences.en: Dr. Frieden was also the New York City Public Health Commissioner under Mayor Bloomberg from 2002 to 2009.
sentences.zh: 弗里登博士还曾在布隆伯格市长任内（2002年至2009年）担任纽约市公共卫生局局长。

sentences.en: And he talks about the difference between running a city health agency and a federal health agency.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了管理城市卫生机构与管理联邦卫生机构之间的区别。

sentences.en: Which one had the most power might surprise you.
sentences.zh: 哪一个权力更大，可能会让你感到惊讶。

sentences.en: But first, Elizabeth is going to take us through Article 2, section by section.
sentences.zh: 但首先，伊丽莎白将带我们逐节梳理第二条的内容。

sentences.en: We covered Article 1 before that was addressing Congress, its powers and limitations.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，我们已经讨论过第一条，即关于国会及其权力和限制的内容。

sentences.en: Now, let's take a brief tour of Article 2.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们简要浏览一下第二条。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: So, Article 2 can be seen as doing a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 第二条可以被视为起到了几个作用。

sentences.en: Specifying the selection of the president and the function of the executive branch.
sentences.zh: 明确总统的选举方式和行政部门的职能。

sentences.en: Listing the specific powers of the president.
sentences.zh: 列举总统的具体权力。

sentences.en: Listing the duties of the president.
sentences.zh: 列举总统的职责。

sentences.en: And what to do with a constitutionally inadequate president.
sentences.zh: 以及如何处理宪法意义上不称职的总统。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, there are some, just like with Article 1, some very important aspects of the executive branch that are in Article 2.
sentences.zh: 就像第一条一样，第二条中也包含了一些行政部门非常重要的方面。

sentences.en: But some things that are not in Article 2 at all, but nevertheless important.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些内容完全不在第二条中，却同样重要。

sentences.en: So, we'll get to those.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们稍后会谈到这些。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But I think the big thing, unlike our discussion about Congress, is that with Article 2, a huge force affecting Article 2 is Trump.
sentences.zh: 但我认为最重要的一点是，与我们讨论国会时不同，影响第二条的一个巨大力量是特朗普。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court's treatment of Trump.
sentences.zh: 以及最高法院对特朗普的处理方式。

sentences.en: Trump has had a very significant impact on how we think about the powers of the presidency.
sentences.zh: 特朗普对我们如何看待总统权力产生了非常重大的影响。

sentences.en: So, let's start with Section 1.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从第一节开始。

sentences.en: Section 1 contains the vesting clause, which says,
sentences.zh: 第一节包含了授予条款，其中写道：

sentences.en: The executive power shall be vested in a president of the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 行政权力应授予美利坚合众国总统。

sentences.en: Now, we saw a vesting clause in Article 1 as well.
sentences.zh: 我们也在第一条中看到了授予条款。

sentences.en: But Article 1 and Article 2 have a notable difference.
sentences.zh: 但第一条和第二条有一个显著的区别。

sentences.en: Article 1 says,
sentences.zh: 第一条写道：

sentences.en: All legislative powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress.
sentences.zh: 本宪法所授予的全部立法权，应授予国会。

sentences.en: Article 2 doesn't refer to just powers herein granted.
sentences.zh: 第二条并没有提到“本宪法所授予的”。

sentences.en: Now, you could say, well, maybe that was just a lapse on the part of the drafters.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会说，这也许只是起草者的一时疏忽。

sentences.en: But maybe not, because that suggests there's some ambiguity as to whether the powers in Article 2 are just examples, or are they the only powers the president has?
sentences.zh: 但也许并非如此，因为这暗示了第二条中的权力究竟只是例子，还是总统拥有的全部权力，这其中存在某种模糊性。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Now, the spoiler, of course, is that every president has said, no, we have more.
sentences.zh: 当然，剧透一下，每一位总统都说，不，我们拥有的权力更多。

sentences.en: We have more than what's in Article 2, right?
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的比第二条中列出的要多，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And practically speaking, we've treated presidents as having some more power than what's specifically laid out in Article 2.
sentences.zh: 从实际操作层面来看，我们确实认为总统拥有的权力比第二条中明确规定的要多。

sentences.en: But, of course, the contested part is always how much power.
sentences.zh: 但当然，争议点始终在于到底有多少权力。

sentences.en: So, that's the opener.
sentences.zh: 这就是开场白。

sentences.en: Section 1 also describes our system of using electors and the Electoral College.
sentences.zh: 第一节还描述了我们使用选举人和选举人团的制度。

sentences.en: Each state appoints electors equal to the number of senators and electors.
sentences.zh: 每个州任命的选举人人数等于该州的参议员和众议员人数之和。

sentences.en: And Article 2 is a compromise, right, between directly electing the president by popular vote or having the president selected by Congress directly.
sentences.zh: 第二条是一种妥协，对吧，是在由普选直接选出总统，还是由国会直接选出总统之间达成的妥协。

sentences.en: There is, of course, a popular vote.
sentences.zh: 当然，确实存在普选。

sentences.en: But when we all vote, we are actually voting for a slate of electors appointed by our state's political parties.
sentences.zh: 但当我们投票时，实际上是在为我们所在州政党提名的选举人名单投票。

sentences.en: And that means the important number is not 51% of everyone voting, but 270 of the 538 electoral votes up for grabs.
sentences.zh: 这意味着重要的数字不是51%的普选票，而是538张选举人票中的270张。

sentences.en: Because of Article 2, a presidential candidate can win the popular vote but lose the electoral college and not become president,
sentences.zh: 由于第二条的存在，总统候选人可能赢得普选票，但输掉选举人团投票，从而无法成为总统，

sentences.en: like Hillary Clinton did in 2016 and Al Gore did in 2000.
sentences.zh: 就像2016年的希拉里·克林顿和2000年的阿尔·戈尔那样。

sentences.en: This system is so central that, of course, we did have a fake electors plot during the 2020 presidential election.
sentences.zh: 这个制度如此核心，以至于在2020年总统大选期间，我们确实发生了一起虚假选举人阴谋。

sentences.en: And that was when Republican officials in several battleground states came up with a scheme to submit fake certificates claiming that Trump actually won in states like Arizona and Georgia.
sentences.zh: 当时，几个摇摆州的共和党官员想出了一个计划，提交虚假证书，声称特朗普实际上在亚利桑那州和佐治亚州等州获胜。

sentences.en: And these were acts designed to overturn the legitimate election of Joe Biden and dozens.
sentences.zh: 这些行为旨在推翻乔·拜登的合法当选，涉及数十人。

sentences.en: It just was so many scandals ago that I forgot this fundamental one that is truly mind-blowing just in and of itself.
sentences.zh: 那已经是太多丑闻之前的事了，我甚至忘记了这个本身就令人震惊的基本丑闻。

sentences.en: If that was the only scandal a president had, that would be enough to disqualify them in my mind.
sentences.zh: 如果那是总统唯一的丑闻，在我看来也足以取消他们的资格了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it was also both dastardly and completely inept.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅卑鄙，而且完全无能。

sentences.en: No one really thought it was going to work.
sentences.zh: 没人真的认为它会成功。

sentences.en: I guess so.
sentences.zh: 我想也是。

sentences.en: So dozens of people have been indicted on these state criminal charges for participating in these fake electors schemes.
sentences.zh: 所以，数十人因参与这些虚假选举人计划而受到州刑事指控。

sentences.en: In fact, the fake electors scheme was part of the criminal conspiracy alleged by special counsel Jack Smith and discussed in the criminal indictment of Trump in 2023.
sentences.zh: 事实上，虚假选举人计划是特别检察官杰克·史密斯指控的刑事阴谋的一部分，并在2023年对特朗普的刑事起诉书中进行了讨论。

sentences.en: And of course, the Supreme Court put an end to that in 2024 with its decision on presidential immunity.
sentences.zh: 当然，最高法院在2024年通过关于总统豁免权的裁决结束了这一切。

sentences.en: And the re-election of Trump ensured that the Justice Department would drop the remainder of the case, which it did.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普的连任确保了司法部会撤销案件的其余部分，事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: Now, Article 2 then addresses the question of succession.
sentences.zh: 接下来，第二条讨论了继任问题。

sentences.en: If something happens to the president, let's say the president dies or somehow is unable to be president anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果总统发生了什么事，比如总统去世或以某种方式无法再担任总统。

sentences.en: And while Article 2 is actually superseded by the 25th Amendment in 1967, after that amendment,
sentences.zh: 虽然第二条实际上在1967年被第25修正案所取代，但在该修正案之后，

sentences.en: there is no question that the vice president becomes the president when the president dies or resigns or does something similar.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，当总统去世、辞职或发生类似情况时，副总统将成为总统。

sentences.en: There was some ambiguity before the 25th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 在第25修正案之前，确实存在一些模糊性。

sentences.en: But now we know for certain that there is vice presidential succession after the president can no longer be president.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们确定，在总统无法再担任总统后，副总统会继任。

sentences.en: The 25th Amendment also gives power to Congress to establish the line of succession what if the vice president dies or can't serve in some other way.
sentences.zh: 第25修正案还赋予国会权力，以确定如果副总统去世或以其他方式无法任职时的继任顺序。

sentences.en: And so just as a little piece of information, the Presidential Succession Act today would mean, in order, you ready?
sentences.zh: 作为一个小知识点，今天的《总统继任法》意味着，按顺序排列，准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, please.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的，请说。

sentences.en: President Vance, President Mike Johnson, President Chuck Grassley, who, by the way, is 92, President Marco Rubio, President Scott Besant, and President Pete Hegseth.
sentences.zh: 万斯总统、迈克·约翰逊总统、查克·格拉斯利总统（顺便说一句，他已经92岁了）、马可·鲁比奥总统、斯科特·贝森特总统和皮特·海格塞斯总统。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Yes, you can pick among all of those people.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可以在这些人中挑选。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That's just, it's purely theoretical, though, purely theoretical.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是理论上的，纯粹是理论上的。

sentences.en: That's so miserable.
sentences.zh: 这太悲惨了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And Article 2 then goes on to talk about the domestic—I know, it's a—
sentences.zh: 第二条接着谈到了国内——我知道，这是一个——

sentences.en: I would just save the list, and I'm just like, okay, it can't get worse, and it can't get worse.
sentences.zh: 我本来想把这个名单存起来，我当时想，好吧，情况不会更糟了，不会更糟了。

sentences.en: And it's like, yeah, I think actually Hegseth would be worse.
sentences.zh: 结果就像是，是的，我觉得海格塞斯当总统会更糟。

sentences.en: You know, like, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像，天哪。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But so many things would have to happen for us to have President Pete Hegseth.
sentences.zh: 但要让我们迎来皮特·海格塞斯总统，需要发生太多事情了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: And let us not wish for any of those things to happen.
sentences.zh: 我们还是别希望这些事情发生吧。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, then Clause 7 of Article 2 contains the Domestic Emoluments Clause.
sentences.zh: 那么，第二条的第7款包含了国内薪酬条款。

sentences.en: Let's go back to this for a second.
sentences.zh: 让我们再回过头来看一下这个。

sentences.en: The president shall not receive any emolument from the United States or any of them.
sentences.zh: 总统不得从美国或任何州获得任何薪酬。

sentences.en: And this is—the plain English of this is the president can't receive any gift from the federal government or any of the state governments.
sentences.zh: 用通俗易懂的话来说，就是总统不能从联邦政府或任何州政府那里接受任何礼物。

sentences.en: This is similar to the Foreign Emoluments Clause, which can actually be found in Article 1,
sentences.zh: 这类似于《外国薪酬条款》，实际上可以在第一条中找到，

sentences.en: which says that no person holding any office of profit or trust accept any emolument from any king, prince, or foreign state without the consent of Congress.
sentences.zh: 该条款规定，任何担任利润或信托职位的人，未经国会同意，不得接受任何国王、王子或外国国家的任何薪酬。

sentences.en: Remember that in Trump's first term, a group of lawsuits were filed alleging that Trump had violated both the foreign and the domestic emoluments clauses.
sentences.zh: 还记得在特朗普的第一个任期内，有人提起了一系列诉讼，指控特朗普违反了外国和国内薪酬条款。

sentences.en: And the basis of their claims was that Trump's continued stake in his business interests had led to some kind of improper influence.
sentences.zh: 他们主张的基础是，特朗普在商业利益中持续持股导致了某种不正当的影响。

sentences.en: So, for example, if a representative of a foreign government was staying at the Trump International Hotel in Washington, D.C.,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果外国政府的代表住在华盛顿特区的特朗普国际酒店，

sentences.en: maybe we could think of that as an improper gift to the president, right?
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以认为这是给总统的不正当礼物，对吧？

sentences.en: We never, of course, found out whether they were unconstitutional emoluments because after Trump left office in 2021, these lawsuits were declared moot,
sentences.zh: 当然，我们永远不知道这些是否属于违宪的薪酬，因为在特朗普2021年离任后，这些诉讼被宣布为无意义，

sentences.en: no longer live issues that a federal court could decide.
sentences.zh: 不再是联邦法院可以裁决的现实问题。

sentences.en: So, we never really got the answer about whether or not these were unconstitutional emoluments.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们从未真正得到关于这些是否属于违宪薪酬的答案。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then emoluments after emoluments.
sentences.zh: 然后是薪酬，还是薪酬。

sentences.en: There's an emolument every hour at this point.
sentences.zh: 现在每小时都有薪酬问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Surprisingly, there haven't been any lawsuits that I'm aware of.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，据我所知，还没有发生任何诉讼。

sentences.en: But, again, we don't know the answer.
sentences.zh: 但同样，我们不知道答案。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, Section 2 of Article 2 specifies the powers of the president.
sentences.zh: 现在，第二条的第二节明确了总统的权力。

sentences.en: Clause 1 tells us that the president is the commander-in-chief of the military, right?
sentences.zh: 第一款告诉我们，总统是军队的总司令，对吧？

sentences.en: So, we have talked a bit about the war power and the fact that in our system, the president, who is a civilian, is in charge of the armed forces.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们已经谈了一些关于战争权的问题，以及在我们的制度中，身为平民的总统负责武装部队的事实。

sentences.en: And that's a very deliberate choice.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常深思熟虑的选择。

sentences.en: So, there are some other powers here.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里还有一些其他权力。

sentences.en: But the other thing I want to mention now is that Section 2 of Article 2 includes the pardon power.
sentences.zh: 但我现在想提到的另一件事是，第二条的第二节包括了赦免权。

sentences.en: Article 2 says that the president shall have power to grant reprieves and pardons for offenses against the United States, except in cases of impeachment.
sentences.zh: 第二条规定，总统有权对违抗美国的罪行给予缓刑和赦免，弹劾案除外。

sentences.en: So, what this means is that the Constitution gives the president broad authority to grant pardons.
sentences.zh: 这意味着宪法赋予了总统广泛的赦免权。

sentences.en: And the only real limits here are that they can only be used for federal criminal offenses.
sentences.zh: 这里唯一真正的限制是，它们只能用于联邦刑事犯罪。

sentences.en: So, you can't use them for state offenses or civil claims of any kind.
sentences.zh: 所以，你不能将它们用于州犯罪或任何形式的民事索赔。

sentences.en: And it cannot be used in cases of impeachment.
sentences.zh: 而且它不能用于弹劾案。

sentences.en: And the president's pardon power is so broad that the Supreme Court has said previously that the power of the presidency is not subject to legislative control.
sentences.zh: 总统的赦免权非常广泛，以至于最高法院此前曾表示，总统的权力不受立法控制。

sentences.en: And there have been, of course, many controversial pardons in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，过去有很多有争议的赦免。

sentences.en: You know, for instance, in 2001, President Clinton pardoned his brother Roger for his conviction on drug offenses.
sentences.zh: 你知道，例如，2001年，克林顿总统赦免了他的兄弟罗杰，因为他犯有毒品罪。

sentences.en: And everyone thought, well, that's just using his influence to help out his family, right?
sentences.zh: 每个人都想，好吧，那只是利用他的影响力来帮助他的家人，对吧？

sentences.en: But Trump is a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普有点不同。

sentences.en: Trump has taken this pardon power much, much further.
sentences.zh: 特朗普将这种赦免权运用得更远、更远了。

sentences.en: So, for instance, on December 1st, Trump pardoned former Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernandez.
sentences.zh: 例如，12月1日，特朗普赦免了前洪都拉斯总统胡安·奥兰多·埃尔南德斯。
zh_words: 胡安·奥兰多·埃尔南德斯

sentences.en: Hernandez, why was he being pardoned?
sentences.zh: 埃尔南德斯，他为什么要被赦免？

sentences.en: He had been sentenced to 45 years in prison for conspiring to import cocaine into the United States.
sentences.zh: 他因密谋向美国输入可卡因而被判处45年监禁。

sentences.en: Why am I mentioning this?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要提这个？

sentences.en: Because this is just months after the administration began to blow up boats in the Caribbean
sentences.zh: 因为这距离政府开始在加勒比海炸毁船只仅几个月，

sentences.en: because it claims that these boats are carrying narco-terrorists smuggling drugs into the United States from Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 因为政府声称这些船只载有从委内瑞拉向美国走私毒品的毒枭恐怖分子。

sentences.en: So, a little bit of an inconsistency there.
sentences.zh: 所以，这有点不一致。

sentences.en: Have they ever spoken to why they did that pardon?
sentences.zh: 他们有没有解释过为什么要进行那次赦免？

sentences.en: Like, even their own story of this?
sentences.zh: 比如，即使是他们自己对此的说法？

sentences.en: You know, just unfair, witch hunt, too long of a sentence, etc.
sentences.zh: 你知道，只是不公平、猎巫行动、刑期太长等等。

sentences.en: And Roger Stone reportedly lobbied the president directly on Hernandez's behalf.
sentences.zh: 据报道，罗杰·斯通直接代表埃尔南德斯向总统进行了游说。

sentences.en: Stone's a longtime Trump advisor.
sentences.zh: 斯通是特朗普的长期顾问。

sentences.en: And apparently it worked.
sentences.zh: 显然这起作用了。

sentences.en: And on January 20th, as one of Trump's very first acts in his second term, there's a pretty significant use of the pardon power.
sentences.zh: 1月20日，作为特朗普第二任期的首批行动之一，赦免权得到了相当重大的使用。

sentences.en: Trump pardoned nearly all of the 1,600 people charged in connection with the attack on the Capitol on January 6th, 2021.
sentences.zh: 特朗普赦免了与2021年1月6日袭击国会大厦有关的近1600名被指控者中的几乎所有人。

sentences.en: Trump also commuted the sentences of 14 members of the Proud Boys and the Oath Keeper groups.
sentences.zh: 特朗普还减免了“骄傲男孩”和“誓言守护者”组织14名成员的刑期。

sentences.en: And commutations are also part of the pardon power.
sentences.zh: 减刑也是赦免权的一部分。

sentences.en: These were folks primarily convicted of seditious conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 这些人主要是因煽动阴谋罪被定罪的。

sentences.en: As part of his pardon order here, Trump also ordered the Justice Department to dismiss all pending indictments against people who were still facing charges for January 6th.
sentences.zh: 作为特朗普赦免令的一部分，他还下令司法部撤销所有针对仍在面临1月6日事件指控的人员的未决起诉。

sentences.en: Now, months later, the Justice Department also took the very broad position that criminal cases that were secondary to the January 6th attacks were also covered by the pardon,
sentences.zh: 几个月后，司法部采取了一种非常宽泛的立场，认为那些与1月6日袭击事件相关的次要刑事案件也属于赦免范围，

sentences.en: although some judges have already rejected these claiMs.
sentences.zh: 尽管一些法官已经驳回了这些主张。

sentences.en: So that's, for instance, they were, after January 6th, let's say investigators were looking for evidence of your involvement in the attacks on the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，假设在1月6日之后，调查人员正在寻找你参与国会大厦袭击事件的证据。

sentences.en: And while they were searching your home, they found illegal firearms or illegal drugs.
sentences.zh: 在搜查你家时，他们发现了非法枪支或非法毒品。

sentences.en: You know, these folks have said, well, you know, I'm covered by this pardon.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些人会说，好吧，我在这项赦免令的覆盖范围内。

sentences.en: And the Justice Department said, well, yeah, sure, because they're somehow related in a very tangential way to investigating your involvement in January 6th,
sentences.zh: 而司法部则表示，好吧，确实如此，因为它们在某种程度上与调查你是否参与1月6日事件有着非常微弱的联系，

sentences.en: which, of course, seems kind of crazy, right?
sentences.zh: 这当然看起来有点疯狂，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: This is a pretty extraordinary use of the pardon power.
sentences.zh: 这是对赦免权相当非同寻常的使用。

sentences.en: I mean, definitely presidents in the past have used a mass pardon power.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，过去的总统当然也使用过大规模赦免权。

sentences.en: But this is of a different order altogether.
sentences.zh: 但这完全是另一个层面的事。

sentences.en: This mass pardon is a political statement by Trump.
sentences.zh: 这次大规模赦免是特朗普的一种政治声明。

sentences.en: This was an attempt to shut down a constitutional process on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 这是试图在1月6日当天阻断宪法程序。

sentences.en: And Trump's really saying these acts are not worthy of punishment, not at all, right?
sentences.zh: 特朗普实际上是在说，这些行为不值得惩罚，一点也不，对吧？

sentences.en: So that seems to be pretty significant.
sentences.zh: 所以这看起来相当重要。

sentences.en: Is there another example of a mass pardon that was sending a political message?
sentences.zh: 还有其他发送政治信息的大规模赦免的例子吗？

sentences.en: If I'm not mistaken, like Carter pardoned all the draft dodgers.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，比如卡特赦免了所有逃避兵役的人。

sentences.en: Right, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But yeah, I mean, for sure, we might say that I'm certain there were people who disagreed with it at the time.
sentences.zh: 但确实，我的意思是，我们肯定可以说，当时肯定有人不同意这一点。

sentences.en: But it's not quite the same political statement, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这并不是完全相同的政治声明，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I think the same idea of mass political pardons.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为大规模政治赦免的理念是一样的。

sentences.en: And, you know, they did, in fact, violate the law.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们确实违反了法律。

sentences.en: But here, you know, you might say that the attack on the Capitol was a kind of attack on the very structure of the democratic process, right?
sentences.zh: 但在这里，你可能会说，对国会大厦的袭击是对民主程序结构本身的一种攻击，对吧？

sentences.en: And Trump's undoing of it, which was well within his power, is a way of saying this is completely fake.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普撤销这一行为——这完全在他的权力范围内——是一种宣称这一切完全是虚假的手段。

sentences.en: There's nothing that they did wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的一切都没有错。

sentences.en: In effect, you know, you could do it all again.
sentences.zh: 实际上，你知道，你可以把这一切再做一遍。

sentences.en: It would be fine.
sentences.zh: 那也没关系。

sentences.en: I mean, that's essentially the message of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这本质上就是它传达的信息。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: There's no punishment whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 没有任何惩罚可言。

sentences.en: Yeah, but you could say that, you know, the structure of the armed forces is, you know, relies on the draft.
sentences.zh: 是的，但你可以说，武装部队的结构是依赖于征兵制的。

sentences.en: And therefore, you know, these people fundamentally undermined that structure.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些人从根本上破坏了那个结构。

sentences.en: And, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道。

sentences.en: True, true.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: That's not, you know, I suppose you could say that.
sentences.zh: 那不是，你知道，我想你可以这么说。

sentences.en: But I think that probably the January 6th attack was of a very different magnitude.
sentences.zh: 但我认为1月6日的袭击在量级上非常不同。

sentences.en: Totally, totally different.
sentences.zh: 完全，完全不同。

sentences.en: I'm not saying it's not different.
sentences.zh: 我不是说它没有区别。

sentences.en: All I'm saying is that you could make a political argument that both of them are undermining the norms of our both political, military, and governmental system.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，你可以提出一个政治论点，即两者都在破坏我们政治、军事和政府体系的规范。

sentences.en: And it certainly was destabilizing to have people avoid the draft and all that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 而且人们逃避兵役之类的事情确实具有破坏稳定性。

sentences.en: No, true, true.
sentences.zh: 不，没错，没错。

sentences.en: Although I think we still would have had a government that was standing.
sentences.zh: 尽管我认为我们仍然会有一个屹立不倒的政府。

sentences.en: Not to only tell me what would have happened if the attack had been successful on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 别只告诉我如果1月6日的袭击成功了会发生什么。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 有道理。

sentences.en: I really would prefer not to think about that.
sentences.zh: 我真的宁愿不去想那个。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: And on December 11th, this is another interesting one, Trump pardoned Tina Peters.
sentences.zh: 12月11日，这是另一个有趣的例子，特朗普赦免了蒂娜·彼得斯。

sentences.en: Peters is a former county clerk in Colorado.
sentences.zh: 彼得斯是科罗拉多州的一名前县书记官。

sentences.en: She's an election fraud conspiraciSt.
sentences.zh: 她是一位选举舞弊阴谋论者。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是啊。

sentences.en: And she was convicted of election interference.
sentences.zh: 她因干扰选举被定罪。

sentences.en: Here's the kicker.
sentences.zh: 重点来了。

sentences.en: I'm not sure what to call this.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么称呼这个。

sentences.en: A symbolic pardon?
sentences.zh: 象征性的赦免？

sentences.en: A nonsensical pardon?
sentences.zh: 荒谬的赦免？

sentences.en: An outrageous pardon?
sentences.zh: 令人愤慨的赦免？

sentences.en: Because, remember, Article 2 gives Trump the authority to pardon someone for an offense against the United States.
sentences.zh: 因为请记住，宪法第二条赋予特朗普赦免某人针对美国所犯罪行的权力。

sentences.en: She was convicted on state charges.
sentences.zh: 她是被州级指控定罪的。

sentences.en: It is absolutely a meaningless pardon.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一个毫无意义的赦免。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: He can say whatever he likes.
sentences.zh: 他想说什么都可以。

sentences.en: And, in fact, I suppose we could say it's not really a pardon at all because it is not permissible for a president to pardon someone on state charges.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想我们可以说这根本算不上赦免，因为总统无权赦免因州级指控而被定罪的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But these are the sorts of things that he's doing, and everyone says, well, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 但这些就是他正在做的事情，每个人都在问，这到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: And the answer is it means nothing.
sentences.zh: 答案是，它什么也不意味着。

sentences.en: If a lawyer was thinking about getting convictions for people who are sympathetic to Trump, usually, or used to be,
sentences.zh: 如果一位律师想让那些同情特朗普的人（通常是，或者曾经是）被定罪，

sentences.en: that the gold standard for getting a conviction is you bring up federal charges because you have the weight of the federal government to prosecute.
sentences.zh: 那么获得定罪的黄金标准就是提出联邦指控，因为你有联邦政府的权力来起诉。

sentences.en: And that's really scary when all of a sudden it's, like, kicked up to the feds.
sentences.zh: 当事情突然被移交给联邦时，那真的很可怕。

sentences.en: It's a big, big, big deal.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非常、非常、非常重大的事情。

sentences.en: But tactically, it makes more sense today to make, you know, some of these things state charges if that's appropriate.
sentences.zh: 但在策略上，如果合适的话，今天将其中一些事情作为州级指控处理更有意义。

sentences.en: Is anyone thinking like that?
sentences.zh: 有人在这样想吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if anyone's thinking like that, but that certainly makes sense at the federal level if you want to avoid federal charges.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是否有人在这样想，但如果你想避免联邦指控，这在联邦层面确实说得通。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's definitely more of a sense that there's perhaps a pay-to-play system in some aspects of the criminal justice system now.
sentences.zh: 现在刑事司法系统的某些方面确实更有可能存在一种“付费换取结果”的系统。

sentences.en: Not just only getting a pardon, but maybe you'll have charges that are dropped or charges that are never brought at all.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是获得赦免，也许你还会面临指控被撤销，或者根本就不会被起诉。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, of course, that is deeply corrupting of the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对刑事司法系统有着极大的腐蚀作用。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, I assume that the flip side could happen as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我假设反过来也可能发生。

sentences.en: You know, not sure anybody would want to admit to that right now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不确定现在有人会想承认这一点。

sentences.en: But, yeah, structurally, the incentives are certainly there.
sentences.zh: 但从结构上讲，激励机制确实存在。

sentences.en: The incentives are there to use state courts to convict someone.
sentences.zh: 利用州法院来给某人定罪的激励机制是存在的。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Although, you know, one example, though, is that if you do that, like if you think about the post-January 6 attempts to prosecute or bring criminal prosecution at the state level,
sentences.zh: 尽管你知道，一个例子是，如果你这样做，比如想想1月6日之后在州一级进行起诉或提出刑事控告的尝试，

sentences.en: look what happened, which was harassment, intimidation of the very prosecutors that we saw in Georgia and elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 看看发生了什么，我们在佐治亚州和其他地方看到的正是对检察官的骚扰和恐吓。

sentences.en: You know, you can try to bring state charges,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以尝试提出州级指控，

sentences.en: but then you have the entire apparatus of the right-wing media and people who – the president himself may call you out and threaten you.
sentences.zh: 但随后你就会面对整个右翼媒体机构，以及那些——总统本人可能会点名威胁你。

sentences.en: So there is that.
sentences.zh: 所以确实存在这种情况。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So then Article 2 goes next to bring in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 接下来宪法第二条引入了参议院。

sentences.en: In Clause 2, the president can make treaties with the advice and consent of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 在第二款中，总统可以在参议院的建议和同意下缔结条约。

sentences.en: So here we now have a partnership with a part of Congress.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在与国会的一部分建立了伙伴关系。

sentences.en: Now, with the advice and consent of the Senate, the president can also appoint ambassadors, Supreme Court justices, and all other officers of the United States.
sentences.zh: 现在，在参议院的建议和同意下，总统还可以任命大使、最高法院大法官以及美国的所有其他官员。

sentences.en: That's why we see televised hearings whenever the president selects new members of his cabinet.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么每当总统挑选新的内阁成员时，我们都会看到电视转播的听证会。

sentences.en: All of the secretaries must be given Senate approval.
sentences.zh: 所有的部长都必须获得参议院的批准。

sentences.en: And the same is true, for instance, of federal judges.
sentences.zh: 联邦法官也是如此。

sentences.en: But there's a more complicated part of this clause, which is called the Appointments Clause.
sentences.zh: 但这一条款中还有一个更复杂的部分，被称为“任命条款”。

sentences.en: Article 2 refers to the president's ability to appoint officers of the United States, but the Congress may, by law,
sentences.zh: 宪法第二条提到了总统任命美国官员的能力，但国会可以通过法律，

sentences.en: vest the appointment of such inferior officers as they think proper in the president alone or in the courts of law or in the heads of departments.
sentences.zh: 将他们认为合适的下级官员的任命权授予总统本人、法院或部门首长。

sentences.en: Now, OK, I've got to say, pretty dry, very boring part of Article 2, right?
sentences.zh: 好了，我得说，这是宪法第二条中非常枯燥、非常无聊的部分，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, it's more confusing than boring.
sentences.zh: 嗯，与其说枯燥，不如说更令人困惑。

sentences.en: Yes, it's very confusing.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常令人困惑。

sentences.en: Not at all obvious to most people what this means or why it's even important, but it is important.
sentences.zh: 对大多数人来说，这到底意味着什么或为什么它很重要一点也不明显，但它确实很重要。

sentences.en: So think of officers as the top people in the executive branch who don't make up the vast majority of federal employees.
sentences.zh: 所以，把官员想象成行政部门的高层人员，他们并不构成绝大多数联邦雇员。

sentences.en: Those folks are in the civil service, right?
sentences.zh: 那些人属于公务员系统，对吧？

sentences.en: They're not appointed by the president.
sentences.zh: 他们不是由总统任命的。

sentences.en: So the Supreme Court has interpreted this part of Article 2 to mean that there are two kinds of officers of the United States, principal officers and inferior officers, OK?
sentences.zh: 所以最高法院将宪法第二条的这一部分解释为，美国有两种官员：主要官员和下级官员，明白吗？

sentences.en: Now, principal officers have to be appointed by the president and confirmed by the Senate.
sentences.zh: 主要官员必须由总统任命并经参议院确认。

sentences.en: So a member of the president's cabinet has to be appointed by the president himself and then confirmed by the Senate.
sentences.zh: 所以总统内阁成员必须由总统本人任命，然后经参议院确认。

sentences.en: Inferior officers can be, but they don't have to be.
sentences.zh: 下级官员可以由总统任命，但不一定非要如此。

sentences.en: They can be appointed by another part of the federal government, right?
sentences.zh: 他们可以由联邦政府的其他部门任命，对吧？

sentences.en: So think of the appointments clause as the hiring clause of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 所以把任命条款看作是宪法的“招聘条款”。

sentences.en: When can the president hire people himself or when can Congress decide, hey, we want some other part of the government to do the hiring of these top executive officials?
sentences.zh: 总统什么时候可以亲自聘用人员，或者国会什么时候可以决定，嘿，我们希望政府的其他部门来聘用这些行政高官？

sentences.en: OK, so that's hiring.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这就是招聘。

sentences.en: Pretty important, right?
sentences.zh: 很重要，对吧？

sentences.en: Who gets to run different aspects of the federal government?
sentences.zh: 谁来负责联邦政府的不同方面？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Now, here's the other aspect.
sentences.zh: 现在，这是另一个方面。

sentences.en: Hiring implies firing, right?
sentences.zh: 招聘意味着解雇，对吧？

sentences.en: That's something we think of, well, presidents can do that, right?
sentences.zh: 这是我们认为总统可以做的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, the problem here is that Article 2 says nothing about when officers can be fired or, to use the constitutional language, be removed from office.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，宪法第二条对官员何时可以被解雇，或者用宪法语言来说，被免职，只字未提。

sentences.en: So what we have is a set of practices in the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一套最高法院的惯例。

sentences.en: Everyone agrees that the president can certainly fire members of his own cabinet for any reason.
sentences.zh: 每个人都同意总统当然可以以任何理由解雇他自己的内阁成员。

sentences.en: The Secretary of Defense, Secretary of State, they can all just be fired because the president just wakes up one day and says, I don't like you.
sentences.zh: 国防部长、国务卿，他们都可以被解雇，因为总统某天醒来后说，我不喜欢你。

sentences.en: You're fired.
sentences.zh: 你被解雇了。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: That's absolutely within the president's power.
sentences.zh: 这完全在总统的权力范围内。

sentences.en: And our guest for later on in today's episode, Tom Frieden, who was director of the CDC, he held a position that could be fired by the president for any reason, any reason at all.
sentences.zh: 我们今天节目稍后的嘉宾汤姆·弗里登，他曾担任疾控中心主任，他所担任的职位可以被总统以任何理由解雇，任何理由都可以。

sentences.en: I don't agree with you or I just don't like you personally.
sentences.zh: 我不赞同你，或者我个人就是不喜欢你。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, historically, Congress has passed laws to protect some officials in the executive branch from being fired by the president for any reason at all.
sentences.zh: 历史上，国会曾通过法律来保护行政部门的一些官员，使其免于被总统以任何理由解雇。

sentences.en: And in other words, they would say, well, this kind of person can only be fired or removed for certain reasons, like they're convicted of a crime or they are obviously incompetent,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们会说，这类人只能因特定原因被解雇或免职，比如他们被判有罪或明显不称职，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So this happens when Congress has decided it would be a good idea for this official to have some independence, to be able to stay in their position,
sentences.zh: 所以这种情况发生在国会认为该官员拥有一定的独立性、能够留在职位上是件好事的时候，

sentences.en: even if the current president disagrees with them.
sentences.zh: 即使现任总统不同意他们的观点。

sentences.en: And the constitutional issue is whether that interferes with the president's Article II authority.
sentences.zh: 而宪法问题在于这是否干扰了总统的宪法第二条权力。

sentences.en: This matters now because the Roberts court has been chipping away at this idea of protecting these folks and giving the president more control over the executive branch and disagreeing with Congress,
sentences.zh: 这之所以重要，是因为罗伯茨法院一直在削弱保护这些人的理念，赋予总统对行政部门更多的控制权，并不同意国会，

sentences.en: providing these folks with some protections.
sentences.zh: 为这些人提供一些保护。

sentences.en: So, for instance, in 2020,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，在2020年，

sentences.en: the Supreme Court decided that Congress's attempt to protect the director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau by restricting the reasons for the president being able to fire them was an unconstitutional interference with the president's authority.
sentences.zh: 最高法院裁定，国会试图通过限制总统解雇理由来保护消费者金融保护局局长的做法，是对总统权力的违宪干扰。

sentences.en: So in plain English, after this case, which is called CELA law, the president can fire the CFPB director for any reason at all.
sentences.zh: 所以用通俗的话说，在这个被称为“塞拉法”的案件之后，总统可以以任何理由解雇消费者金融保护局局长。

sentences.en: And that's why on February 1st of this year, Trump fired Rohit Chopra, who had been appointed by Biden and confirmed by the Senate.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在今年2月1日，特朗普解雇了罗希特·乔普拉，他曾由拜登任命并经参议院确认。

sentences.en: Just don't like you.
sentences.zh: 就是不喜欢你。

sentences.en: You're gone.
sentences.zh: 你被解雇了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that's despite what Congress had tried to do, try to protect this person because they should have some independence in, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管国会曾试图采取行动，试图保护这个人，因为他们理应在某些方面保持独立，你知道的，

sentences.en: creating the rules and enforcing the regulations to help consumers.
sentences.zh: 在制定规则和执行法规以帮助消费者方面。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And now the Supreme Court is definitely not done with this issue.
sentences.zh: 而现在，最高法院显然还没有处理完这个问题。

sentences.en: This Supreme Court is now considering what is very likely going to be a very important case.
sentences.zh: 最高法院目前正在审理一起极有可能非常重要的案件。

sentences.en: It asks, can Trump simply fire a member of the Federal Trade Commission, the FTC,
sentences.zh: 它提出了一个问题：特朗普能否直接解雇联邦贸易委员会（FTC）的一名成员，

sentences.en: even though Congress has tried through legislation to provide some protection for commissioners of the FTC?
sentences.zh: 尽管国会已试图通过立法为联邦贸易委员会的委员提供某种保护？

sentences.en: Now, if the Supreme Court decides to allow Trump to do this, this means trouble not just for the FTC,
sentences.zh: 如果最高法院决定允许特朗普这样做，这意味着不仅对联邦贸易委员会，

sentences.en: but the job protections for many other federal commissions and boards that are within the executive branch.
sentences.zh: 而且对行政部门内许多其他联邦委员会和机构的工作保障来说，都将是麻烦的开始。

sentences.en: These are the agencies meant to protect consumers, workers, the environment, all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 这些机构旨在保护消费者、工人和环境等各类事物。

sentences.en: So what is the argument that Trump can do this, you know, when they were specifically designed to be independent and laws were passed to ensure their independence?
sentences.zh: 那么，特朗普可以这样做的论据是什么呢？毕竟这些机构是专门设计为独立的，而且法律也已通过以确保它们的独立性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in one way, it's not just Trump.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，这不仅仅是特朗普的问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a longstanding conservative movement that was building long before Trump assumed office.
sentences.zh: 这是一个长期存在的保守派运动，早在特朗普就职之前就已经在酝酿了。

sentences.en: But the conservative argument and Trump's argument is that everybody, every single person within the executive branch should be within the control of the president.
sentences.zh: 但保守派的论点，也是特朗普的论点，即行政部门内的每一个人，每一个个体，都应该处于总统的控制之下。

sentences.en: Otherwise, they're totally unaccountable.
sentences.zh: 否则，他们就完全不受问责。

sentences.en: Now, I mean, that's kind of silly, right, because they're accountable in lots of different ways.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点荒谬，对吧？因为他们可以通过许多不同的方式被问责。

sentences.en: But that's the conservative argument.
sentences.zh: 但这正是保守派的论点。

sentences.en: And it's one that the Supreme Court might adopt in this case that I've mentioned.
sentences.zh: 而且这很可能是最高法院在上述案件中可能采纳的观点。

sentences.en: And it's pretty clear that the Supreme Court is very interested in this question because this is not the only case that they are considering this term.
sentences.zh: 很明显，最高法院对这个问题非常感兴趣，因为这并不是他们本届任期内审理的唯一相关案件。

sentences.en: This term, the Supreme Court will also consider whether Trump can fire a member of the Federal Reserve, Lisa Cook.
sentences.zh: 本届任期内，最高法院还将审议特朗普是否有权解雇联邦储备委员会成员丽莎·库克（Lisa Cook）。

sentences.en: She had been appointed by Biden for a 14-year term, which is the regular term, right?
sentences.zh: 她是由拜登任命的，任期为14年，这是常规任期，对吧？

sentences.en: But Trump said, I want to fire you, right?
sentences.zh: 但特朗普说，我想解雇你，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: So one of the big problems here is that you have a conservative majority on the court.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的一个大问题是，法院里存在一个保守派多数派。

sentences.en: And remember, the Roberts Court has been around now for 20 years, right?
sentences.zh: 记住，罗伯茨法院（Roberts Court）现在已经存在20年了，对吧？

sentences.en: The conservative majority on the Roberts Court wants to be protective of a very particular view of presidential power.
sentences.zh: 罗伯茨法院的保守派多数派希望保护一种非常特定的总统权力观。

sentences.en: Let presidents fire agency heads whenever they want and fill them with the choices of whatever they want, right?
sentences.zh: 让总统想解雇机构负责人就解雇，并随心所欲地填补他们想要的人选，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: On the other hand, when agencies in a Democratic administration issue decisions, they also seem to be targets for the Supreme Court to say, oh, no, no,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，当民主党政府下的机构做出决定时，它们似乎也成了最高法院的目标，法院会说，哦，不，不，

sentences.en: you're not allowed to do that, right?
sentences.zh: 你们不允许这样做，对吧？

sentences.en: You've exceeded your powers.
sentences.zh: 你们越权了。

sentences.en: So it turns out that agencies can't win either way.
sentences.zh: 所以结果就是，这些机构无论怎么做都赢不了。

sentences.en: Either they do things that the Supreme Court says you've exceeded your authority, or when they try to be working within that power, then a Republican president, Trump, will say,
sentences.zh: 要么他们做的事情被最高法院说成是越权，要么当他们试图在职权范围内工作时，共和党总统特朗普就会说，

sentences.en: well, I don't like these policies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不喜欢这些政策。

sentences.en: You're fired.
sentences.zh: 你被解雇了。

sentences.en: So the Supreme Court really just seems to be saying everything is within the control of the president,
sentences.zh: 所以最高法院似乎真的只是在说，一切都在总统的控制之下，

sentences.en: and the president can dictate everything that happens within the executive branch.
sentences.zh: 总统可以支配行政部门内发生的一切。

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好的，好的。

sentences.en: So we saw this, like, you know, in terms of the agency stuff, we saw this during the height of the pandemic, with the court striking down vaccine mandates, the eviction moratorium,
sentences.zh: 我们看到了这一点，你知道，就机构事务而言，我们在疫情最严重的时候看到了这一点，当时法院推翻了疫苗强制令、驱逐禁令，

sentences.en: even expanded student loan forgiveness was something that really got its start from the inability of borrowers to pay during the worst part of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 甚至扩大后的学生贷款减免计划，其起因也是借款人在疫情最严重期间无力偿还贷款。

sentences.en: Those are a series of agency actions.
sentences.zh: 这些都是一系列的机构行动。

sentences.en: Biden, during his administration, wanted these things to happen.
sentences.zh: 拜登在执政期间希望这些事情发生。

sentences.en: Even they begin with Trump, too, right?
sentences.zh: 甚至它们也是从特朗普时期开始的，对吧？

sentences.en: But nope, for the Supreme Court, that was too much for an agency to do.
sentences.zh: 但不，对于最高法院来说，这对一个机构来说做得太多了。

sentences.en: And so agency power seems to be attacked from every single angle under the Roberts court theory of, you know, how the executive branch should be run.
sentences.zh: 因此，在罗伯茨法院关于行政部门应如何运作的理论下，机构权力似乎正从各个角度受到攻击。

sentences.en: Is there consistency in the decisions, you know, of that set of things of what an agency can do?
sentences.zh: 这些决定之间有连贯性吗，关于机构能做什么的那一系列事情？

sentences.en: Or does that seem to be dependent on who the president is?
sentences.zh: 还是说这似乎取决于谁是总统？

sentences.en: Seems to be strangely dependent on who the president is, right?
sentences.zh: 似乎奇怪地取决于谁是总统，对吧？

sentences.en: Because, well, you know, a Republican president tends to roll back regulations.
sentences.zh: 因为，嗯，你知道，共和党总统倾向于撤销法规。

sentences.en: That doesn't seem to be a problem for the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 这对最高法院来说似乎不是问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But in a Democratic administration, an agency that tends to provide more enforcement, more regulation, that always turns out to be a bridge too far.
sentences.zh: 但在民主党政府中，一个倾向于提供更多执法、更多监管的机构，总是被认为走得太远了。

sentences.en: Not always, but often.
sentences.zh: 不总是，但经常如此。

sentences.en: And, of course, the blame is, well, why are you doing this extreme set of regulation?
sentences.zh: 当然，指责是，嗯，你们为什么要进行这种极端的监管？

sentences.en: Congress didn't allow you to do this.
sentences.zh: 国会没有允许你们这样做。

sentences.en: Or if Congress wanted you to do this, they should be more specific.
sentences.zh: 或者如果国会想让你们这样做，他们应该更具体一点。

sentences.en: Of course, Congress made the choice to give these agencies a lot of power.
sentences.zh: 当然，国会做出了选择，赋予了这些机构很大的权力。

sentences.en: Maybe it wasn't this particular Congress, but it was the institutional body of Congress that said, well, we don't really know what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 也许不是这一届特定的国会，但国会作为一个机构主体曾说，嗯，我们真的不知道我们在做什么。

sentences.en: Let's give the authority to the agency.
sentences.zh: 让我们把权力交给机构吧。

sentences.en: So you said that there were a set of laws that were passed by Congress to establish kind of independence and term limits for all these different agencies and to have that kind of control.
sentences.zh: 所以你说过国会通过了一系列法律，为所有这些不同的机构建立了某种独立性和任期限制，并拥有那种控制权。

sentences.en: And through these cases, is the Supreme Court determining that, like, all of those laws are basically unconstitutional and thus far just haven't been tested?
sentences.zh: 通过这些案件，最高法院是否在判定，比如，所有这些法律基本上都是违宪的，只是到目前为止还没有经过测试？

sentences.en: Well, not necessarily that the agencies themselves are unlawful, but just that the president has total control over the person at the top of these agencies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不一定是说机构本身不合法，而是说总统对这些机构的最高负责人拥有完全的控制权。

sentences.en: Or increasingly, a form of agency authority that folks had thought were more protected or in less danger were multi-member boards that had staggered terms,
sentences.zh: 或者，人们原本认为更受保护或危险较小的一种机构权力形式，正日益受到威胁，那就是拥有交错任期的多成员委员会，

sentences.en: often with bipartisan membership.
sentences.zh: 通常由两党成员组成。

sentences.en: And that board was supposed to outlast any one particular presidential term.
sentences.zh: 而那个委员会本应比任何特定的总统任期都长。

sentences.en: Well, it seems like even that, too, is going to be vulnerable in some way if the Supreme Court during this term is going to be cutting away at those protections even further.
sentences.zh: 嗯，看起来即使是这一点，如果最高法院在本届任期内要进一步削弱这些保护，也会以某种方式变得脆弱。

sentences.en: And that just means that, of course, whatever an agency does, you just get whipsawed every time there's a new administration.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，当然，无论一个机构做什么，只要有新政府上台，你就会陷入反复无常的境地。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, there has been this notion of building these agencies out to be apolitical bodies in a certain way,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一直有一种理念，即把这些机构建设成某种程度上的非政治性机构，

sentences.en: to have a certain consistency in mission and execution and follow through and vision that would, you know, maybe be shaped by a president somewhat in the agenda of a president,
sentences.zh: 在使命、执行、后续行动和愿景上保持某种一致性，这些可能会受到总统的一定影响，在总统的议程中有所体现，

sentences.en: but wouldn't completely be altered.
sentences.zh: 但不会完全被改变。

sentences.en: And, you know, depending on who the president was.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，取决于谁是总统。

sentences.en: And it seems like now the Supreme Court wants all of these agencies to basically just be arms of the president and follow the whims of the president, the current president.
sentences.zh: 现在看起来最高法院希望所有这些机构基本上都只是总统的延伸，并遵循总统，即现任总统的突发奇想。

sentences.en: Well, that's right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错。

sentences.en: And in particular, if you have a president who decides, in the case of Trump in a second term, that some agencies just shouldn't be agencies.
sentences.zh: 特别是，如果你有一位总统决定，以特朗普第二任期为例，某些机构根本就不应该存在。

sentences.en: There's not much to argue about if you completely got the agency.
sentences.zh: 如果你完全废除了该机构，那就没什么可争论的了。

sentences.en: You know, there's no argument about this has gone too far.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没有关于这是否做得太过的争论。

sentences.en: The agency basically is so crippled that it can't do any work.
sentences.zh: 该机构基本上瘫痪了，无法开展任何工作。

sentences.en: Well, we have to take a quick break, but when we come back, on to Section 3 of Article 2.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们得休息一下，但回来后，我们将讨论第二条第三款。

sentences.en: Section 3.
sentences.zh: 第三款。

sentences.en: Section 3 talks about the duties of the president.
sentences.zh: 第三款谈到了总统的职责。

sentences.en: And, of course, we've talked before in a previous episode about the take care clause.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们之前在上一集中讨论过“忠实执行条款”（take care clause）。

sentences.en: Article 2 says the president—
sentences.zh: 第二条说总统——

sentences.en: Can I ask you a quick question?
sentences.zh: 我可以问你一个简短的问题吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I've asked you this probably years and years ago.
sentences.zh: 我可能多年前就问过你这个问题。

sentences.en: Who is the person who decides what the names of the clauses are?
sentences.zh: 是谁决定了这些条款的名称？

sentences.en: You know, like the take care clause is one thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如“忠实执行条款”是一回事。

sentences.en: Like, I know that language brought it out, but like, you know, like you could call it—
sentences.zh: 比如，我知道语言把它带出来了，但就像，你知道，你可以叫它——

sentences.en: The faithfully executed clause?
sentences.zh: “忠实执行条款”？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or, you know, instead of the vested clause, it could be the power clause.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，与其叫“归属条款”，不如叫“权力条款”。

sentences.en: Or it could be, you know, like, who's the one who—like, who starts that convention and then who picks it up and determines that that that is what you call a clause?
sentences.zh: 或者可能是，你知道，谁是那个——谁开启了那个惯例，然后谁又采纳了它并确定那就是你所说的条款？

sentences.en: Uh, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 呃，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: It just becomes kind of like tribal knowledge of people who work in con law.
sentences.zh: 它只是变成了宪法法领域工作的人的一种部落知识。

sentences.en: You know, like, everybody—every society has its argo, has its lingo, its slang.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像每个社会都有它的行话、术语、俚语一样。

sentences.en: And, like, for in constitutional law, that's the slang, right?
sentences.zh: 在宪法法中，这就是俚语，对吧？

sentences.en: We know you're not part of the in-group if you don't know what's called the take care clause.
sentences.zh: 我们知道如果你不知道什么是“忠实执行条款”，你就不是圈内人。

sentences.en: That's the way I'd put it, right?
sentences.zh: 我会这么说，对吧？

sentences.en: I just wonder who is the—what was the first clause named in the Constitution, you know?
sentences.zh: 我只是好奇谁是——宪法中命名的第一个条款是什么，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: Not sure, but definitely, you're right.
sentences.zh: 不确定，但你肯定是对的。

sentences.en: They each have specific names.
sentences.zh: 它们每个都有特定的名称。

sentences.en: So, this is the take care clause.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是“忠实执行条款”。

sentences.en: The president shall take care that the laws be faithfully executed.
sentences.zh: 总统应确保法律得到忠实执行。

sentences.en: Interestingly enough, this is not in the part of the powers of the president.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这并不在总统权力的部分。

sentences.en: It's one of their duties, right?
sentences.zh: 这是他们的职责之一，对吧？

sentences.en: It's both an emphasis that the executive branch enforces the law.
sentences.zh: 这既强调了行政部门执行法律。

sentences.en: That's the will of Congress.
sentences.zh: 那是国会的意志。

sentences.en: And it's a type of constraint, too, that the president isn't allowed to legislate in any form, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是一种约束，即总统不允许以任何形式立法，对吧？

sentences.en: Now, if you think about the president can't legislate, that's sort of basic high school civic stuff.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你认为总统不能立法，那是基本的高中公民课内容。

sentences.en: But what about executive orders?
sentences.zh: 但是行政命令呢？

sentences.en: I'm sure you've heard of those, right?
sentences.zh: 我相信你听说过那些，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They certainly feel like legislation.
sentences.zh: 它们确实感觉像是立法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But Article 2 says nothing about executive orders.
sentences.zh: 但第二条对行政命令只字未提。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And Congress has no general federal statute that says, hey, president, you can issue executive orders.
sentences.zh: 而且国会没有任何通用的联邦法规说，嘿，总统，你可以发布行政命令。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, it's still generally accepted that presidents have the authority to issue some executive orders.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，人们普遍接受总统有权发布一些行政命令。

sentences.en: Now, usually executive orders are directed at executive officials within the executive branch.
sentences.zh: 通常，行政命令是针对行政部门内的行政官员的。

sentences.en: So it's kind of like the president telling the members of the executive branch what to do.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像总统告诉行政部门的成员该做什么。

sentences.en: So if they're not in here, how are they legal?
sentences.zh: 那么如果它们不在这里面，它们怎么合法呢？

sentences.en: And why can't the Supreme Court come in just like just completely invalidate every executive order that's ever been given?
sentences.zh: 为什么最高法院不能介入，就像完全废除有史以来发布的所有行政命令一样？

sentences.en: Well, who knows at this point?
sentences.zh: 嗯，谁知道呢，现在。

sentences.en: They could do that.
sentences.zh: 他们可以那样做。

sentences.en: But to be legal, a president's executive order either comes from Congress giving the president some power under federal law, or alternatively,
sentences.zh: 但要合法，总统的行政命令要么来自国会在联邦法律下赋予总统的某种权力，或者，

sentences.en: the power can come from the president saying, I'm just using my Article 2 power.
sentences.zh: 权力可以来自总统说，我只是在行使我的第二条权力。

sentences.en: So for the first example, in Trump's first term, remember he issued a proclamation called 9645 that was also known as the Muslim travel ban.
sentences.zh: 所以对于第一个例子，在特朗普的第一任期，记得他发布了一个名为9645的公告，也被称为穆斯林旅行禁令。

sentences.en: That was denying entry into the United States of folks from several majority Muslim countries.
sentences.zh: 那是拒绝来自几个穆斯林占多数国家的民众进入美国。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court upheld Trump's executive order.
sentences.zh: 最高法院维持了特朗普的行政命令。

sentences.en: And its reason was that Congress, when it passed the Immigration and Nationality Act, gave Trump broad authority about when and whether to suspend the entry of non-citizens.
sentences.zh: 其理由是，国会在通过《移民与国籍法》时，赋予了特朗普关于何时以及是否暂停非公民入境的广泛权力。

sentences.en: And of course, Trump was doing just that, maybe for improper, subjectively horrible reasons, but he was simply doing what Congress allowed him to do.
sentences.zh: 当然，特朗普当时正是这样做的，也许是出于不当的、主观上可怕的原因，但他只是在做国会允许他做的事情。

sentences.en: So the court says that's an OK executive order.
sentences.zh: 所以法院说那是一个合法的行政命令。

sentences.en: As for an executive order that is based on constitutional authority, Truman gives us an example.
sentences.zh: 至于基于宪法权力的行政命令，杜鲁门给了我们一个例子。

sentences.en: When Truman desegregated the armed forces in 1948, he did so through an executive order.
sentences.zh: 当杜鲁门在1948年废除武装部队的种族隔离时，他是通过行政命令做到的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And how did he do that?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: He said his authority came not just from federal statutes, but from his authority as commander in chief.
sentences.zh: 他说他的权力不仅来自联邦法规，还来自他作为三军统帅的权力。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: That makes the most sense to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说最有意义。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Anything within the military makes the most sense to me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，军事领域内的一切都最合乎逻辑。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Now, a big aspect of Trump's second term is just the sheer number of executive orders that he has issued.
sentences.zh: 现在，特朗普第二任期的一个重要方面就是他发布了数量惊人的行政命令。

sentences.en: So to give you a sense, in his first term, Trump issued 220 executive orders total.
sentences.zh: 为了让你有个概念，在第一任期内，特朗普总共发布了220项行政命令。

sentences.en: So far, it's just December of 2025.
sentences.zh: 而现在才2025年12月。

sentences.en: In his second term, Trump has issued at least, I think, 218.
sentences.zh: 在第二任期内，我想特朗普已经发布了至少218项。

sentences.en: That was as of October.
sentences.zh: 那是截至10月份的数据。

sentences.en: And of course, the first year isn't even over yet.
sentences.zh: 当然，第一年还没过完呢。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I know there was another one just yesterday.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道就在昨天又发布了一项。

sentences.en: Some of these are just ordinary or they seem to be symbolic, but others have tried to dramatically change how we understand how the federal government works.
sentences.zh: 其中一些只是常规操作，或者看起来具有象征意义，但另一些则试图彻底改变我们对联邦政府运作方式的理解。

sentences.en: So targeting law firms that represent Democrats, ending climate and energy initiatives, freezing foreign aid, and, of course, ending birthright citizenship.
sentences.zh: 比如针对代理民主党人的律师事务所、终止气候和能源倡议、冻结对外援助，当然，还有终止出生公民权。

sentences.en: Now, just because the president issues an executive order doesn't mean it's legal, of course, and dozens of Trump's executive orders have already been challenged in court.
sentences.zh: 当然，总统发布行政命令并不意味着它就合法，特朗普的数十项行政命令已经受到了法律挑战。

sentences.en: So how can an order be challenged then?
sentences.zh: 那么，一项命令该如何被挑战呢？

sentences.en: Well, the easiest way is when a later president revokes the executive order.
sentences.zh: 最简单的方法就是由后任总统撤销该行政命令。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So like a succeeding president just says, all of that is undone.
sentences.zh: 就像继任总统直接宣布，之前的一切作废。

sentences.en: And that happens all the time.
sentences.zh: 这种情况经常发生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: When Biden became president, he revoked many of Trump's orders from his first term.
sentences.zh: 拜登就任总统时，撤销了特朗普第一任期的许多命令。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then when Trump became president, he revoked a huge number of Biden's orders from his term.
sentences.zh: 然后特朗普就任总统时，又撤销了拜登任期内的大量命令。

sentences.en: Now, in his first two months in office, Trump revoked 91 of Biden's executive orders.
sentences.zh: 在就职后的头两个月里，特朗普撤销了拜登的91项行政命令。

sentences.en: That's just a lot comparatively.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，这数量确实很大。

sentences.en: Sixty-seven of Biden's executive orders were revoked in one executive order.
sentences.zh: 拜登的67项行政命令是在一份行政命令中被一次性撤销的。

sentences.en: He just like wanted to wipe out everything that Biden had done.
sentences.zh: 他就像是想抹掉拜登所做的一切。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: That was a first, actually.
sentences.zh: 这其实还是头一遭。

sentences.en: So many in one executive order.
sentences.zh: 在单一行政命令中撤销这么多项。

sentences.en: Now, Congress can't overturn.
sentences.zh: 国会是无法推翻的。

sentences.en: If I became president after Trump, not only would I nullify every executive order, I think I would tear down every building he touched.
sentences.zh: 如果我在特朗普之后当选总统，我不仅会废除他所有的行政命令，我想我还会拆掉他经手过的每一栋建筑。

sentences.en: Well, unfortunately, that's going to be a – I'm not sure if that's a harder task or an easier task.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不幸的是，这可能是一项——我不确定这到底是更难还是更容易的任务。

sentences.en: Well, Congress can't overturn an executive order because it's really something that the president is just doing.
sentences.zh: 国会无法推翻行政命令，因为这本质上是总统个人的行为。

sentences.en: But if the president is claiming that the reason why he can issue an order is because he's implementing a statute,
sentences.zh: 但如果总统声称他发布命令的理由是执行某项法规，

sentences.en: then Congress can simply modify or negate the order by passing another law themselves.
sentences.zh: 那么国会可以通过自行通过另一项法律来简单地修改或否定该命令。

sentences.en: No, that's not what we meant at all.
sentences.zh: 不，我们根本不是那个意思。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: And of course, if there's a constitutional problem, lawsuits can be filed alleging that there are legal constitutional problems with the order, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，如果存在宪法问题，可以提起诉讼，声称该命令存在法律和宪法问题，对吧？

sentences.en: And that – we've seen that in – again, there are dozens of lawsuits right now.
sentences.zh: 而且我们已经看到了——再说一次，现在有几十起诉讼。

sentences.en: If the power to give executive orders is not in there, how do you begin to argue that he doesn't have the power to do a certain thing?
sentences.zh: 如果行政命令的权力不在宪法里，你该如何论证他没有权力做某件事呢？

sentences.en: It just seems like it's all kind of weirdly in the clouds.
sentences.zh: 这看起来就像是悬在半空中，非常奇怪。

sentences.en: It's – it is.
sentences.zh: 确实是这样。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, I mean, part of constitutional practice, of course, is always history.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，宪法实践的一部分当然始终包含历史因素。

sentences.en: And, you know, George Washington had an executive order.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，乔治·华盛顿也有过行政命令。

sentences.en: So we have lived with something that is arguably constitutional because everyone has always agreed that it's constitutional for the president to do this kind of thing,
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直生活在某种可以说合乎宪法的事物中，因为大家都一致认为总统做这类事情是符合宪法的，

sentences.en: not the specific versions of them.
sentences.zh: 而不是指具体的版本。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, presidents are allowed to do this.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，总统还是被允许这样做。

sentences.en: Now, in modern presidencies, unfortunately, it becomes a way for a frustrated president to try to regulate when Congress will not do so.
sentences.zh: 在现代总统任期内，不幸的是，当国会不作为时，这成了受挫的总统试图进行监管的一种方式。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: But they're always very temporary because the next administration will tend to modify or revoke completely many executive orders.
sentences.zh: 但这些命令通常非常短暂，因为下一届政府往往会修改或彻底撤销许多行政命令。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So now let's step back for a moment.
sentences.zh: 那么现在让我们退后一步。

sentences.en: Article 2 tells us that the president of the United States has some very important powers that are just for the president alone.
sentences.zh: 宪法第二条告诉我们，美国总统拥有一些非常重要的权力，这些权力仅属于总统个人。

sentences.en: The president has the duty to execute federal law.
sentences.zh: 总统有执行联邦法律的职责。

sentences.en: The president commands the armed forces.
sentences.zh: 总统统帅武装部队。

sentences.en: The president grants pardons, appoints officers of the United States, and negotiates treaties.
sentences.zh: 总统有权给予赦免、任命美国官员以及协商条约。

sentences.en: The Constitution gives this one person in the federal government all of this power.
sentences.zh: 宪法将所有这些权力赋予了联邦政府中的这一个人。

sentences.en: So the question is, how do we ensure that the president, as Hamilton wrote in the Federalist Papers, is not a feeble executive?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，我们如何确保总统——正如汉密尔顿在《联邦党人文集》中所写的那样——不会成为一个软弱的行政长官？

sentences.en: How do we make sure that the president isn't hampered too much and can act in the way that Article 2 intended?
sentences.zh: 我们如何确保总统不会受到过多阻碍，并能按照第二条的意图行事？

sentences.en: Well, in 2024, of course, the Supreme Court's answer was immunity from criminal prosecution.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在2024年，最高法院的答案当然是刑事起诉豁免权。

sentences.en: So we've done an episode on this previously, but remember that in August of 2023, Special Counsel Jack Smith concluded his investigation.
sentences.zh: 我们之前做过一期关于这个的节目，但请记住，2023年8月，特别检察官杰克·史密斯结束了他的调查。

sentences.en: A federal grand jury indicted Trump, who was not president at the time, on a four-count indictment related to what happened after he lost the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 一个联邦大陪审团起诉了特朗普，当时他并非总统，起诉书包含四项罪名，与他输掉2020年大选后发生的事情有关。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So this includes the fake electorate scheme, pressuring state officials, attempting a sham Justice Department investigation,
sentences.zh: 这包括虚假选举人计划、向州官员施压、试图进行虚假的司法部调查，

sentences.en: leaning on Vice President Pence to change the election certification on January 6th, and making public statements about election fraud.
sentences.zh: 在1月6日向副总统彭斯施压要求改变选举认证结果，以及就选举舞弊发表公开声明。

sentences.en: So the monumental decision in Trump versus the United States was simply summarized like this.
sentences.zh: 因此，特朗普诉美国案中那项具有里程碑意义的裁决，简单总结如下：

sentences.en: A president cannot be prosecuted for much of this conduct.
sentences.zh: 总统不能因大部分此类行为而被起诉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Specifically for unofficial conduct, the Supreme Court said that's fine.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，对于非官方行为，最高法院表示没问题。

sentences.en: A president can be prosecuted for things that have nothing to do with the office of the presidency.
sentences.zh: 总统可以因与总统职位无关的事情而被起诉。

sentences.en: But when it comes to official conduct, the Supreme Court said that the president's official acts can be divided into two parts.
sentences.zh: 但当涉及官方行为时，最高法院表示总统的官方行为可以分为两部分。

sentences.en: So sort of imagine a circle.
sentences.zh: 试着想象一个圆圈。

sentences.en: At the edge of the circle are official acts that aren't related to a core presidential power.
sentences.zh: 圆圈边缘是与核心总统权力无关的官方行为。

sentences.en: And so there, the president enjoys a presumption of immunity from prosecution that the prosecution can overcome in limited circumstances.
sentences.zh: 在那里，总统享有起诉豁免的推定，检方只能在有限的情况下才能推翻这种推定。

sentences.en: But that included a lot of conduct, including, according to the Supreme Court, speaking to and on behalf of the American people.
sentences.zh: 但这包括了许多行为，据最高法院称，甚至包括代表美国人民发表讲话。

sentences.en: And at the time, that was a lot of tweeting, right?
sentences.zh: 当时，那可是发了大量的推文，对吧？

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then there's the center of the circle.
sentences.zh: 然后是圆圈的中心。

sentences.en: At the center of the circle, you have official conduct that the Supreme Court called core constitutional functions.
sentences.zh: 在圆圈中心，是最高法院所称的“核心宪法职能”的官方行为。

sentences.en: What are they?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: The powers that we've just talked about.
sentences.zh: 就是我们刚才谈到的那些权力。

sentences.en: The pardon power.
sentences.zh: 赦免权。

sentences.en: The power to remove or fire officers of the United States.
sentences.zh: 罢免或解雇美国官员的权力。

sentences.en: And importantly for the criminal prosecution of Trump, the investigation and prosecution of crimes.
sentences.zh: 以及对特朗普刑事起诉至关重要的——对犯罪行为的调查和起诉。

sentences.en: So in the Supreme Court's view, even if this was a complete bogus and sham investigation, when Trump directed the Justice Department to say, hey, look into election fraud.
sentences.zh: 所以按照最高法院的观点，即使这是一场完全虚假和伪造的调查，当特朗普指示司法部说，嘿，去调查选举舞弊时，

sentences.en: Well, that was core Article 2 conduct.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是核心的第二条行为。

sentences.en: Therefore, it can't be prosecuted, even if it's based on bad faith, even if it was made up.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使它是基于恶意，即使它是编造的，也不能被起诉。

sentences.en: And as for the other conduct that might not have enjoyed total immunity, the outer part of that circle,
sentences.zh: 至于其他可能不享有完全豁免权的行为，也就是圆圈外围的部分，

sentences.en: remember the Supreme Court decision in Trump versus the United States came out on July 1st, 2024.
sentences.zh: 请记住，最高法院在特朗普诉美国案中的裁决是在2024年7月1日做出的。

sentences.en: The court took so long in deciding the case that time ran out.
sentences.zh: 法院在审理此案时花费了太长时间，以至于时间耗尽了。

sentences.en: Trump was reelected and then the case disappeared.
sentences.zh: 特朗普再次当选，然后案件就不了了之了。

sentences.en: But the impact of Trump versus the United States and core Article 2 conduct is just really enormous.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普诉美国案和核心第二条行为的影响确实非常巨大。

sentences.en: You know, we've talked previously about the Trump administration's use of the military for these boat strikes to blow up alleged drug smuggling boats in the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们之前谈到过特朗普政府利用军队进行这些船只打击，炸毁加勒比海地区涉嫌走私毒品的船只。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, the administration claims that they're in a war with these drug smugglers, and that's why the boats can be blown up without any process.
sentences.zh: 嗯，政府声称他们与这些毒贩处于战争状态，这就是为什么可以在没有任何程序的情况下炸毁这些船只。

sentences.en: But of course, as we've discussed before, this doesn't seem to be a war at all.
sentences.zh: 但当然，正如我们之前讨论过的，这看起来根本不是战争。

sentences.en: And in fact, the decision to kill without arrest or trial has been characterized by many serious legal analysts as murder, just plain simple murder.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种不经逮捕或审判就杀人的决定，被许多严肃的法律分析人士定性为谋杀，纯粹的谋杀。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So what if it is murder?
sentences.zh: 那么如果是谋杀又怎样？

sentences.en: After all, Trump is the commander in chief under Article 2.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，特朗普是第二条下的三军统帅。

sentences.en: Well, I think the pretty clear answer from the 2024 decision is that as long as Trump is exercising a core Article 2 constitutional power,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为2024年的裁决给出的答案很明确：只要特朗普是在行使核心的第二条宪法权力，

sentences.en: he himself cannot be criminally prosecuted, even if the evidence suggests that these boat strikes amount to murder.
sentences.zh: 他本人就不能被刑事起诉，即使证据表明这些船只打击等同于谋杀。

sentences.en: Does that mean everyone around him is immune as well?
sentences.zh: 那是否意味着他周围的所有人也享有豁免权？

sentences.en: No, this was only a decision about the president himself.
sentences.zh: 不，这只是关于总统本人的裁决。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So everyone around him could go down for murder and he would stand alone as the person was on.
sentences.zh: 所以他周围的人可能会因谋杀罪被判刑，而他会作为唯一一个没事的人独善其身。

sentences.en: I mean, but possibly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有可能。

sentences.en: I mean, of course, the Supreme Court was only deciding the question of the president.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，最高法院当时只裁决了关于总统的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's just interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真有意思。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。
