sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Also, there was that crazy hypothetical from the immunity case.
sentences.zh: 另外，豁免权案中还有一个疯狂的假设。

sentences.en: Before the case was actually decided by the Supreme Court, one of the judges on the appeals court panel raised this SEAL Team 6 hypothetical.
sentences.zh: 在最高法院实际做出裁决之前，上诉法院小组的一位法官提出了这个“海豹突击队6队”的假设。

sentences.en: SEAL Team 6 is that elite group of Navy SEALs that carry out high stakes military missions, right?
sentences.zh: 海豹突击队6队是执行高风险军事任务的精英海豹突击队，对吧？

sentences.en: Judge Florence Pan, who was on the appeals court in D.C., asked Trump's lawyer, could a president order SEAL Team 6 to assassinate a political rival?
sentences.zh: 华盛顿特区上诉法院的法官弗洛伦斯·潘问特朗普的律师，总统能否命令海豹突击队6队暗杀政治对手？

sentences.en: That's an official act.
sentences.zh: 那是一项官方行为。

sentences.en: Trump's lawyer, John Sauer, would not give a direct answer.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的律师约翰·绍尔没有给出直接回答。

sentences.en: Well, The Washington Post reported at the end of November, who carried out the boat strikes?
sentences.zh: 嗯，《华盛顿邮报》在11月底报道说，是谁执行了船只打击任务？

sentences.en: SEAL Team 6, right?
sentences.zh: 海豹突击队6队，对吧？

sentences.en: It's just a weird hypothetical come to real life.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个变成现实的奇怪假设。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And then there's Section 4 of Article 2.
sentences.zh: 还有第二条的第四款。

sentences.en: That is impeachment.
sentences.zh: 那就是弹劾。

sentences.en: Section 4 is supposed to be a remedy, right?
sentences.zh: 第四款本应是一种补救措施，对吧？

sentences.en: It tells us that the president, the vice president, and all civil officers of the United States shall be removed from office on impeachment for and conviction of treason, bribery,
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们，总统、副总统和所有美国文职官员在因叛国、贿赂、

sentences.en: or other high crimes and misdemeanors.
sentences.zh: 或其他严重罪行和轻罪被弹劾并定罪后，应被免职。

sentences.en: In 2021, President Trump became the only president in American history to be impeached twice and, in fact, in the same term.
sentences.zh: 2021年，特朗普总统成为美国历史上唯一一位被弹劾两次的总统，而且事实上，是在同一个任期内。

sentences.en: The first impeachment trial arose from the call he made to a Ukrainian president, Zelensky, right,
sentences.zh: 第一次弹劾审判源于他与乌克兰总统泽连斯基的通话，对吧，

sentences.en: which he was apparently offering to unfreeze military aid if Zelensky would investigate Joe Biden and promote this bogus theory that Russia was not behind the foreign interference in the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 他显然提出如果泽连斯基调查乔·拜登并宣扬俄罗斯并非2016年大选外国干预幕后黑手这一虚假理论，就解冻军事援助。

sentences.en: And the second impeachment trial accused Trump of incitement to insurrection over the January 6th Capitol attack.
sentences.zh: 第二次弹劾审判指控特朗普因1月6日国会大厦袭击事件而煽动叛乱。

sentences.en: In both Senate trials, Trump was, of course, acquitted.
sentences.zh: 在两次参议院审判中，特朗普当然都被判无罪。

sentences.en: So I think the main takeaway here today is that when there's Article 2, there's no question that Trump, as a president, as an ex-president, and now a president again,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为今天的主要收获是，当涉及到第二条时，毫无疑问，特朗普作为总统、前总统，以及现在再次成为总统，

sentences.en: has left a definitive mark about how we think about Article 2.
sentences.zh: 已经对我们如何看待第二条留下了决定性的印记。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And the Roberts court has also led to a completely different view of Article 2.
sentences.zh: 而罗伯茨领导的最高法院也导致了对第二条完全不同的看法。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, this is fascinating stuff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些内容太迷人了。

sentences.en: I'm so glad we went through Article 2 in greater depth.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们更深入地探讨了第二条。

sentences.en: And what great fortune it is to have President Trump to guide us through this moment of exploration.
sentences.zh: 有特朗普总统引导我们度过这一探索时刻，真是太幸运了。

sentences.en: We have survived one year.
sentences.zh: 我们挺过了一年。

sentences.en: We'll see what happens next year.
sentences.zh: 看看明年会发生什么吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't even know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我甚至都不知道。

sentences.en: I don't even know.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都不知道。

sentences.en: Coming up, our conversation with former CDC director, Dr. Tom Frieden.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将与前疾控中心主任汤姆·弗里登博士进行对话。

sentences.en: Now our conversation with Dr. Tom Frieden, a physician and public health expert.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们与医生兼公共卫生专家汤姆·弗里登博士进行对话。

sentences.en: Today, he's the executive director of the global health nonprofit Resolve to Save Lives and author of the recent book, The Formula for Better Health, How to Save Millions of Lives,
sentences.zh: 如今，他是全球健康非营利组织“拯救生命决心”的执行主任，也是近期出版的《更好健康的公式：如何拯救数百万生命》一书的作者，

sentences.en: Including Your Own.
sentences.zh: 包括你自己的生命。

sentences.en: He was the 16th director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention under President Obama from 2009 to 2017,
sentences.zh: 他曾在奥巴马总统任内（2009年至2017年）担任第16任美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）主任，

sentences.en: which makes him the second longest serving head in the CDC's history.
sentences.zh: 这使他成为CDC历史上任职时间第二长的负责人。

sentences.en: Before that, Dr. Frieden was the New York City public health commissioner under Mayor Bloomberg from 2002 to 2009.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，弗里登博士曾于2002年至2009年间在布隆伯格市长任内担任纽约市公共卫生局局长。

sentences.en: So he has experience at both the city and the federal level.
sentences.zh: 所以他在城市和联邦层面都有丰富的经验。

sentences.en: Dr. Frieden, thank you so much for being on the show.
sentences.zh: 弗里登博士，非常感谢您来到我们的节目。

sentences.en: Great to join you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能参加。

sentences.en: So Article 2 establishes the executive branch and assumes that the president will have a cabinet.
sentences.zh: 美国宪法第二条确立了行政分支，并假定总统将拥有一个内阁。

sentences.en: But what the drafters of Article 2 did not contemplate is the growth of what we call the administrative state, the many,
sentences.zh: 但第二条的起草者们没有预见到我们所谓的“行政国家”的增长，即今天联邦政府中众多的、

sentences.en: many agencies in the federal government today that regulate everything from food that is safe to eat and water that is clean to drink, working conditions that are fair,
sentences.zh: 众多的机构，它们监管着从安全的食品和清洁的饮用水，到公平的工作条件，

sentences.en: corporate behavior that is honest for consumers.
sentences.zh: 以及对消费者诚实的企业行为等一切事务。

sentences.en: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is one of the roughly dozen agencies housed within the Department of Health and Human Services.
sentences.zh: 疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）是隶属于卫生与公众服务部的大约十几个机构之一。

sentences.en: The origins of the CDC go back to 1942.
sentences.zh: CDC的起源可以追溯到1942年。

sentences.en: It's a pretty interesting history.
sentences.zh: 它的历史相当有趣。

sentences.en: It was a wartime agency called the Office of Malaria Control in War Areas.
sentences.zh: 它最初是一个战时机构，名为“战区疟疾控制办公室”。

sentences.en: Then it became Communicable Disease Center in 1946 and then Centers for Disease Control in 1980.
sentences.zh: 后来在1946年更名为“传染病中心”，并在1980年更名为“疾病控制与预防中心”。

sentences.en: In part because of those unusual origins, the CDC acquires its powers from different sources.
sentences.zh: 部分由于这些不同寻常的起源，CDC的权力来源各不相同。

sentences.en: Congress has directly given the CDC some of its powers, but some of the CDC's powers have been delegated to it from the Secretary of Health and Human Services.
sentences.zh: 国会直接赋予了CDC部分权力，但CDC的一些权力是由卫生与公众服务部部长下放给它的。

sentences.en: And from the Surgeon General.
sentences.zh: 还有来自卫生局局长的授权。

sentences.en: For example, the CDC has the power to issue quarantine orders because it has been delegated those powers by the Surgeon General,
sentences.zh: 例如，CDC有权发布检疫令，因为这些权力是由卫生局局长下放给它的，

sentences.en: who in turn was given those powers from the Federal Public Health Service Act of 1944.
sentences.zh: 而卫生局局长的这些权力又是根据1944年的《联邦公共卫生服务法》获得的。

sentences.en: So it's a long way of giving a little bit of a preamble of where those constitutional powers of the CDC come from.
sentences.zh: 所以，这算是为CDC这些宪法权力的来源做了一个冗长的铺垫。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Frieden, I'm hoping you can tell us.
sentences.zh: 那么，弗里登博士，我希望您能告诉我们。

sentences.en: This agency, you know, began as a way to stop malaria from spreading among the military, but it does so much more than that now.
sentences.zh: 这个机构最初是为了阻止疟疾在军队中传播，但现在它所做的远不止于此。

sentences.en: Could you describe the objectives of the CDC today?
sentences.zh: 您能描述一下CDC今天的目标吗？

sentences.en: Quite simply, what the CDC has traditionally done is to work 24-7 to protect Americans from threats, whether those threats are natural or man-made,
sentences.zh: 简单来说，CDC传统上所做的工作就是全天候（24/7）保护美国人免受威胁，无论这些威胁是自然的还是人为的，

sentences.en: whether they are infectious diseases or otherwise, whether they come from the United States or anywhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 无论它们是传染病还是其他疾病，也无论它们是来自美国境内还是世界任何地方。

sentences.en: That's the bottom line.
sentences.zh: 这就是核心所在。

sentences.en: Healthier, safer people.
sentences.zh: 让人们更健康、更安全。

sentences.en: So, the CDC and the entire federal government faced a gigantic health threat in 2020 with the COVID pandemic.
sentences.zh: 那么，CDC和整个联邦政府在2020年新冠疫情期间面临着巨大的健康威胁。

sentences.en: And during that first term of the Trump administration, the CDC wasn't insulated from political pressure.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普政府的第一任期内，CDC并没有与政治压力隔绝。

sentences.en: And there were a lot of criticism, experts criticized, the different sort of calculation of risk.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多批评，专家们批评了那种对风险的不同计算方式。

sentences.en: When it comes to this agency, which is within the executive branch and therefore sort of like under the president,
sentences.zh: 当谈到这个属于行政分支、因此某种程度上受总统管辖的机构时，

sentences.en: but has its own expertise and its own guidelines and its own thoughts on things,
sentences.zh: 但它又拥有自己的专业知识、指导方针和对事物的见解，

sentences.en: what is the right balance for agency like the CDC to respond to what the president might want versus what is best for public health?
sentences.zh: 对于像CDC这样的机构来说，在响应总统的需求与坚持公共卫生最佳利益之间，正确的平衡点在哪里？

sentences.en: I go back to a couple of core concepts here.
sentences.zh: 我想回到几个核心概念上。

sentences.en: The analyst and thinker about government, James Q.
sentences.zh: 政府分析师和思想家詹姆斯·Q·威尔逊等人曾讨论过“专业人士”的定义。

sentences.en: Wilson and others have talked about what is the definition of a professional.
sentences.zh: 专业人士是指那些拥有独立于其组织指挥链之外的标准的人。

sentences.en: And a professional is someone who has standards that are outside of the line of control, the line of command of their group.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为一名医生，如果我在一个组织工作，而我的上级要求我开这种药或做这项检查，但这与我的专业责任不符，

sentences.en: So, as a physician, if I'm working in an organization and my supervisor says, give this medicine or get this test, and that's inconsistent with my professional responsibility,
sentences.zh: 我必须拒绝，否则我就违反了我的专业责任。

sentences.en: I have to say no or I have to violate my professional responsibility.
sentences.zh: 同样地，CDC试图提供清晰、一致、基于事实的信息，明确指出：这是我们所知的，这是我们所不知的，

sentences.en: In the same way, the CDC tries to provide clear, consistent, fact-based information, making clear, this is what we know, this is what we don't know,
sentences.zh: 这是我们得出结论的方法。

sentences.en: this is how we know what we know.
sentences.zh: 第二件需要理解的大事是——我认为政治分歧各方中的许多人都误解了这一点——CDC的角色不是制定政策。

sentences.en: And the second big thing to understand that I think a lot of people have gotten wrong on all sides of the political divide is that the CDC's role is not to set policy.
sentences.zh: CDC的角色是为那些制定政策的人提供信息：如果你做X，你就会得到Y。

sentences.en: The CDC's role is to inform those who set policy, if you do X, you will get Y.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要，因为例如，如果你谈论口罩之类的问题，如果每个人在新冠病毒广泛传播时在室内都佩戴口罩，

sentences.en: This is really important because, for example, if you talk about something like masks, if everyone wears masks indoors when COVID is spreading widely,
sentences.zh: 新冠病毒的传播就会减少。

sentences.en: there will be less spread of COVID.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说每个人都应该一直戴着口罩，或者我们应该关闭所有餐馆或酒吧。

sentences.en: That's not saying that everyone should wear masks indoors all the time or we should close all the restaurants or we should close the bars.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这最好留给社区，通过社区讨论和当地民选领导人来决定。

sentences.en: This is something that we think is best left to communities to decide with a community discussion and elected leaders of that community.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为一个科学型组织的本质是，它能公开、客观地基于现有的最佳科学证据提供有效信息。

sentences.en: So I think the essence of a science-based organization is that it provides valid information based on the best available scientific evidence openly and objectively derived.
sentences.zh: CDC最引人注目的部分之一是该机构发布的建议。

sentences.en: One of the most visible parts of the CDC is recommendations that come from the agency.
sentences.zh: 这些建议涵盖了从疫苗指南到医院和医生办公室的手部卫生等方方面面。

sentences.en: And these can be anything from vaccine guidelines to hand hygiene in hospitals and doctor's offices.
sentences.zh: 这种关于建议的沟通是单向的吗？还是说CDC确定的建议被提交给政策制定者，然后政策制定者会说，嗯，你知道，

sentences.en: Is that communication for recommendations one way or is the recommendation for what the CDC has determined put forward to policymakers and policymakers go, well, you know,
sentences.zh: 这是可能的。

sentences.en: this is possible.
sentences.zh: 这是不可能的。

sentences.en: This is not possible.
sentences.zh: 这是可行的。

sentences.en: This is feasible.
sentences.zh: 这是不可行的。

sentences.en: This is not feasible.
sentences.zh: 然后你们再考虑到这些反馈，重新调整模型，共同商定出一个方案？

sentences.en: And then you go, you know, rejigger your models with that in mind and then sort of come up with a sort of thing together.
sentences.zh: 还是说这真的只是单向沟通，你们提出建议，然后他们按自己的意愿去执行？

sentences.en: Or is it really just a one-way communication where you present proposals and then they implement it as they see fit?
sentences.zh: 对话的很大一部分是与那些最熟悉特定主题事实的人进行的，以确定什么是适宜的。

sentences.en: The larger part of the dialogue is with the people who are most familiar with the facts about specific topics to say, you know, what is indicated?
sentences.zh: 什么是不适宜的？

sentences.en: What is not indicated?
sentences.zh: 有时很简单明了。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's plain and simple.
sentences.zh: 比如，让你的孩子仰卧睡觉。

sentences.en: You know, put your child on their back to sleep.
sentences.zh: 如果你想降低婴儿猝死综合征（SIDS）的风险。

sentences.en: If you want to reduce the risk of SIDS.
sentences.zh: 直截了当。

sentences.en: Straightforward.
sentences.zh: 而在其他时候，证据并不那么明确，无论是关于营养还是体育锻炼。

sentences.en: Other times, the evidence isn't so clear, whether it's about nutrition or physical activity.
sentences.zh: 比如，剧烈运动有多重要？

sentences.en: You know, how important is vigorous physical activity?
sentences.zh: 体育锻炼的最低剂量是多少？

sentences.en: What's the minimum dose of physical activity?
sentences.zh: 这些都是复杂的话题。

sentences.en: These are complicated topics.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，当涉及到政策选择或建议选择时，更广泛的对话既发生在CDC内部，

sentences.en: So I think when it comes to policy choices or recommendation choices, the bigger dialogue is both within CDC
sentences.zh: 也发生在CDC与卫生与公众服务部的其他部门、联邦政府的其他部门、学术界、倡导者之间，

sentences.en: and among CDC and other parts of the Department of Health and Human Services, other parts of the federal government, academia, advocates,
sentences.zh: 以及其他人之间，以了解什么是真正的事实，从而得出最有效的政策建议。

sentences.en: and others to understand what's really the fact here that's going to lead to a policy recommendation that will be most effective.
sentences.zh: 在政策实施方面，那是另一种科学。

sentences.en: In terms of policy implementation, that's kind of a different science.
sentences.zh: 这可能涉及国会拨款，并说，好吧，CDC，

sentences.en: That may involve Congress allocating money and saying, okay, CDC,
sentences.zh: 给各州和城市拨款，让他们选择是否实施这个项目，或者以他们选择的方式去实施。

sentences.en: give money to states and cities to implement this program if they choose to do so or in the way they choose to do so.
sentences.zh: 有时，你会得到一个利用这些联邦资金来激励地方采取更健康政策的项目。

sentences.en: Occasionally, you'll get a program that uses those federal dollars to incentivize localities to have healthier policies.
sentences.zh: 经典的例子——虽然不是CDC的，但属于联邦政府——是道路安全，各州可以自由选择是否接受联邦资金。

sentences.en: And the classic example of that, not part of CDC, but federal government, is road safety where states were free to take or not take the federal dollars.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们接受了联邦资金，他们就必须降低血液酒精浓度标准，并暂时实行更低的限速。

sentences.en: But if they took the federal dollars, they needed to reduce the blood alcohol concentration and go to lower speed limits for a while.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为公众有时感到困惑的一点是：好吧，也许我确实想依赖专业知识，但依赖谁的专业知识？

sentences.en: So I think one of the things that is sometimes confusing to the public is, well, maybe I do want to rely on expertise, but who's expertise?
sentences.zh: 如果我们转向现任政府，免疫咨询委员会（ASIP）已经彻底改组了。

sentences.en: So if we turn to the current administration, there's been a complete overturning of ASIP, the committee that advises the CDC on immunization.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有前任成员都被卫生与公众服务部部长肯尼迪撤换了，现在有了新的成员。

sentences.en: You know, all of the former members were removed by HHS Secretary Kennedy, and there are new ones.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看名单，如果我是一个普通公众，我会想，嗯，他们看起来资历不错。

sentences.en: But if you look at the list, if I'm a member of the public, I think, well, they seem to be well credentialed.
sentences.zh: 所以也许你能解释一下，拥有良好资历与真正能够就疫苗等问题提供可靠的专家建议之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: So maybe you could explain what is the difference between being well credentialed and actually being able to provide reliable expert advice on something like vaccines?
sentences.zh: 我认为我们国家正面临一个严峻的局面，即“专家”这个词已经变成了一个贬义词。

sentences.en: I think we have a challenging situation in this country where the word expert has become a dirty word.
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因是人们不希望有人说：“我是专家，我知道你应该怎么做。”

sentences.en: And I think part of that is because people don't want someone saying, I'm the expert and I know what you should do.
sentences.zh: 这非常令人反感。

sentences.en: That's very offensive.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是从这句话开始：你们才是你们自己的专家，但科学能做的是，如果你想在健康方面实现某种目标，我们可以告诉你什么是经过验证的，

sentences.en: So I always start with saying, you are the experts in you, but what science can do is it can tell you if you want to achieve something health-wise, we can tell you what's proven,
sentences.zh: 什么是未经证实的。

sentences.en: what's unproven.
sentences.zh: 我认为当谈到确定性水平时，理解这一点非常重要：在一些高度专业化的领域，有些事情几乎是肯定的，

sentences.en: And I think when it comes to levels of certainty, it's really important to understand that there are highly specialized areas where there are things that are virtually certain,
sentences.zh: 这并不难；有些领域完全没有证据，这也不难。

sentences.en: not such a hard thing, where there are things where it's no evidence, not so hard.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个灰色地带，即使在某些领域，仅仅说“我大部分时间都在研究某一个特定的健康问题”也是非常重要的。

sentences.en: It's in that gray zone where it's so important, even in areas where, just to say, I work a huge proportion of my time on one particular health issue.
sentences.zh: 关于那个问题的一篇新文章发表了。

sentences.en: A new article comes out on that.
sentences.zh: 我仍然不是判断那篇文章是否有效的最佳人选。

sentences.en: I'm still not the best person to understand whether that article is valid.
sentences.zh: 我知道我可以去找那些一生都在研究这个问题的人。

sentences.en: I know who I can go to who are people who have worked on this for whole lifetimes.
sentences.zh: 这就是CDC如此出色或曾经如此出色的原因之一。

sentences.en: And that's one of the things that CDC is so wonderful about or has been so wonderful about.
sentences.zh: 那里有这样的人，如果你随意翻开医学教科书的任何一页，那里都有人能告诉你，哦，

sentences.en: There are people there, if you opened a medical textbook to any random page, there have been people there who would be able to tell you, oh,
sentences.zh: 关于这个话题，真正重要的是这些。

sentences.en: here's what's really important about that topic.
sentences.zh: 人们曾问我，我是否怀念担任CDC主任的日子？

sentences.en: And people have asked me, do I miss being CDC director?
sentences.zh: 我怀念的是，当《新英格兰医学杂志》或其他报纸或医学期刊发表文章时，

sentences.en: And what I miss is when an article comes out in the New England Journal of Medicine or some other newspaper or a medical journal,
sentences.zh: 我可以打电话给该领域的世界级专家之一，问他们：“你知道，这到底是怎么回事？”

sentences.en: I could call up one of the world's experts in that area and say, you know, what's the real deal here?
sentences.zh: 所以那种专业知识是深厚的专业知识。

sentences.en: So that kind of expertise is deep expertise.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有一种叫“布兰多里尼定律”（Brandolini's Law）的东西，即揭穿胡言乱语所需的时间比传播它要长得多。

sentences.en: And, you know, there is something called Brandolini's Law, that it takes infinitely longer to debunk nonsense than to spread it.
sentences.zh: 我见过这种情况，例如小罗伯特·肯尼迪（RFK Jr.）所说的一些事情。

sentences.en: And I've seen this, for example, with some of the things that RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 例如，他录制了一个三分钟的视频，宣布美国退出全球疫苗免疫联盟（Gavi）。

sentences.en: is saying.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可怕的错误。

sentences.en: For example, he recorded a three-minute video when he announced that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这意味着许多孩子可能会死于可预防的疾病。

sentences.en: is pulling out of the Global Vaccine Alliance, what's called Gavi.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果这些疾病传播并来到美国，美国可能会面临更大的风险，因为我们无法将疾病拒之门外。

sentences.en: And this is a terrible mistake.
sentences.zh: 病毒不需要签证。

sentences.en: This means that lots of kids may die of preventable disease.
sentences.zh: 在这个三分钟的视频里，他说了多处谎言。

sentences.en: It means the U.S.
sentences.zh: 其中一些，我对问题了解得足够清楚，明白为什么那是谎言。

sentences.en: may be at greater risk if these diseases spread and come here because we can't keep diseases out.
sentences.zh: 但有一个问题，你知道，真的非常复杂。

sentences.en: Viruses don't need visas.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，这种疫苗增加了儿童的死亡率。

sentences.en: And in this three-minute video, he had multiple falsehoods.
sentences.zh: 我花了好几天才追踪到那篇文章。

sentences.en: And some of them, I understood the issue well enough to understand why it was a falsehood.
sentences.zh: 他提到了那篇文章。

sentences.en: But there was one that was, you know, really complicated.
sentences.zh: 而且在大学里，没有人会因为揭穿一篇糟糕的文章而获得晋升，对吧？

sentences.en: He said, oh, this vaccine increases the deaths of children.
sentences.zh: 所以这篇文章在文献中存在了多年。

sentences.en: And it took me days to track down the article.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它曾以一种温和的方式受到过批评。

sentences.en: He mentioned that article.
sentences.zh: 但我花了好几天时间仔细研究才明白，哦，它有一个根本性的方法论缺陷，即未接种疫苗的女孩也有未被记录的死亡。

sentences.en: And then nobody gets promoted in their university for debunking a bad article, right?
sentences.zh: 所以看起来不给这些女孩接种疫苗反而救了她们的命。

sentences.en: So this article was in the literature for years.
sentences.zh: 但它真正显示的是，这些女孩既没有获得医疗服务来接种疫苗，也没有被记录死亡。

sentences.en: You know, it had been criticized in a kind of gentle way.
sentences.zh: 所以有时在谎言的狂风暴雨中追踪真相是非常困难的。

sentences.en: But it took a couple of days to look carefully and understand, oh, it's got a fundamental methodological flaw where the unvaccinated girls also had unrecorded deaths.
sentences.zh: 是的，这不仅仅是谎言，还有确定性与不确定性之间的区别。

sentences.en: So it looked like not vaccinating these girls resulted in saving their lives.
sentences.zh: 科学在不确定性中生活得非常自在，而政治则不然。

sentences.en: But what it really showed was that the girls were neither accessing health care to get vaccines nor having their deaths recorded.
sentences.zh: 当你谈论这个专业原则清单时，你知道，我很高兴听到它们。

sentences.en: So sometimes it's very hard to track down the reality amid a blizzard of falsehoods.
sentences.zh: 它们不一定与政治机构共享。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's also not just falsehoods, but also like the difference between certainty and uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 所以当这些东西必须互动时——而且它们必然会互动——你知道，这种结果的摩擦是什么？

sentences.en: Science lives very comfortably in uncertainty and politics does not.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的观点。

sentences.en: And when you're talking about something, you know, this professional list of principles, you know, I loved hearing them.
sentences.zh: 部分原因与科学教育有关。

sentences.en: They are not shared with necessarily a political body.
sentences.zh: 部分原因与鼓励人们在生活中拥抱细微差别有关。

sentences.en: And so when those things have to interact and necessarily they do have to interact, you know, what is the friction of that outcome?
sentences.zh: 我曾参加过一个焦点小组，成员是对接种疫苗持犹豫态度的人。

sentences.en: I think that's a really important point.
sentences.zh: 他们中的几个人一直说：“就告诉我底线是什么。”

sentences.en: And partly it has to do with science education.
sentences.zh: 而底线是，它会随着时间而改变。

sentences.en: Partly it has to do with encouraging people to embrace nuance in our lives.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么沟通如此重要，我们必须对人们非常清楚。

sentences.en: I was part of a focus group with people who were reluctant to get vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 我们知道什么？

sentences.en: And several of them kept saying, just, you know, tell me the bottom line.
sentences.zh: 我们是如何知道的？

sentences.en: And the bottom line is that it changes over time.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道什么？

sentences.en: And that's why communication is so important, that we are really clear with people.
sentences.zh: 我们正在做什么来试图找出答案？

sentences.en: What do we know?
sentences.zh: 基于我们现在所知的——这可能会改变——这就是我们的建议。

sentences.en: How do we know it?
sentences.zh: 我们挺过了一年。

sentences.en: What do we not know?
sentences.zh: 看看明年会发生什么吧。

sentences.en: What are we doing to try to find it out?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我甚至都不知道。

sentences.en: And based on what we know now, and this may change, this is what we recommend.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都不知道。

sentences.en: And to have some degree of certainty in that.
sentences.zh: 而且要对此有一定程度的把握。

sentences.en: So there's an interesting paradox when it comes to public health and in that sort of step is that any appropriate action when it actually prevents something will feel like an overreaction because it has prevented the thing that it was intending to prevent.
sentences.zh: 公共卫生领域存在一个有趣的悖论，即当采取适当行动成功预防了某事时，它反而会让人觉得是反应过度，因为它已经阻止了原本打算预防的事情发生。

sentences.en: How do you get people to believe in a preventative action doing its job when the result is things are going along swimmingly and they don't, you know, like if it's doing,
sentences.zh: 当预防措施行之有效，一切进展顺利，人们感觉不到它的存在时，你该如何让他们相信这些预防措施发挥了作用呢？

sentences.en: if when government is working well and when the CDC is working well, people should not notice its existence.
sentences.zh: 如果政府和疾控中心（CDC）运作良好，人们本不该注意到它们的存在。

sentences.en: But you need them to notice its existence for it to continue healthfully.
sentences.zh: 但为了让这种健康状态持续下去，你又需要让他们意识到它们的存在。

sentences.en: Like what, how do you deal with that?
sentences.zh: 比如，你该如何处理这种情况？

sentences.en: My organization, Resolve to Save Lives, produces a periodic report called Epidemics That Didn't Happen, where we highlight the great work of a team of doctors, nurses,
sentences.zh: 我的组织“拯救生命决心”（Resolve to Save Lives）会定期发布一份名为《未发生的流行病》的报告，我们在其中重点介绍了世界各地医生、护士团队的伟大工作，

sentences.en: public health specialists somewhere in the world that stopped an epidemic that we never heard about.
sentences.zh: 以及那些我们从未听说过的、成功阻止了流行病的公共卫生专家。

sentences.en: And part of it is emphasizing the progress.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分工作就是强调这些进展。

sentences.en: It's part of human nature to kind of take for granted the things that aren't probleMs.
sentences.zh: 人类的天性就是把那些没有出问题的事情视为理所当然。

sentences.en: And yes, public health generally is not recognized because when we succeed, nothing happens.
sentences.zh: 是的，公共卫生工作通常不被认可，因为当我们成功时，什么都不会发生。

sentences.en: And when we fail, it's headline news.
sentences.zh: 而当我们失败时，那就会成为头条新闻。

sentences.en: Now, of course, then there are also epidemics that do happen.
sentences.zh: 当然，现实中确实也会发生流行病。

sentences.en: And of course, COVID was kind of that thunderclap, that moment of cataclysm.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，新冠疫情就像一声惊雷，是一个灾难性的时刻。

sentences.en: And one response from the federal government during the pandemic was to put a moratorium or a pause on evictions around the country when many people couldn't work.
sentences.zh: 疫情期间，联邦政府的一项应对措施是在全国范围内实施驱逐禁令或暂停驱逐，当时许多人无法工作。

sentences.en: And this was to prevent homelessness in ways that might spread the virus even further.
sentences.zh: 这是为了防止无家可归现象，因为那可能会导致病毒进一步传播。

sentences.en: Now, that moratorium first began in a kind of regular way with Congress approving of the moratorium.
sentences.zh: 起初，这项禁令是以一种常规方式开始的，即由国会批准。

sentences.en: But when Congress failed to renew it,
sentences.zh: 但当国会未能续期时，

sentences.en: it was actually the CDC that used its own authority to issue the moratorium in 2021 because federal law gives the CDC the authority to enforce regulations that are necessary to prevent the spread of communicable diseases.
sentences.zh: 实际上是疾控中心在2021年动用了自己的权力发布了这项禁令，因为联邦法律赋予了疾控中心执行必要法规以防止传染病传播的权力。

sentences.en: So the moratorium was ultimately challenged in court and the Supreme Court put a halt to it the same year that it was issued.
sentences.zh: 后来，这项禁令在法庭上受到挑战，最高法院在禁令发布同一年叫停了它。

sentences.en: Now, this was after your time as director.
sentences.zh: 这发生在你卸任局长之后。

sentences.en: But, you know, we were wondering when you head an agency like the CDC, when you have to make a really big decision like this,
sentences.zh: 但我们想知道，当你领导像疾控中心这样的机构，当你必须做出如此重大的决定时，

sentences.en: do you think primarily and only about the public health decisions?
sentences.zh: 你考虑的主要是且仅仅是公共卫生的决策吗？

sentences.en: Or are you also thinking, well, I have a kind of a legal framework in my mind, too, to make sure that this, if it is to be challenged,
sentences.zh: 还是说你也在想，我脑子里也得有一个法律框架，以确保如果这件事受到挑战，

sentences.en: maybe we can have some safe assumptions about it going forward?
sentences.zh: 我们未来能有一些稳妥的假设？

sentences.en: So I'm not a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 我不是律师。

sentences.en: I'm a doctor.
sentences.zh: 我是一名医生。

sentences.en: I will say that I found some of the regulatory approaches used during COVID, during both the Trump and Biden administrations of CDC not to be appropriate.
sentences.zh: 我得说，我认为在新冠疫情期间，特朗普和拜登政府时期疾控中心所采取的一些监管方法并不恰当。

sentences.en: And I think they were kind of inevitable because Congress didn't act.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这在某种程度上是不可避免的，因为国会没有采取行动。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So because there was a failure to act on the part of Congress,
sentences.zh: 所以，正是因为国会未能采取行动，

sentences.en: CDC authorities were used in ways they had never been used before on both the eviction moratorium and on some immigration issues that probably haven't stood up to legal review.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心的权力被以从未有过的方式使用，无论是驱逐禁令还是某些移民问题，这些做法可能都经不起法律审查。

sentences.en: But your question is a broader one.
sentences.zh: 但你的问题更广泛。

sentences.en: And I think always public health should consider as broad a set of risks and benefits as possible.
sentences.zh: 我认为公共卫生部门始终应该尽可能全面地考虑各种风险和收益。

sentences.en: There's a misconception, I think, that CDC didn't consider, oh, what harm will it be to the economy or to education if there are closures?
sentences.zh: 我认为有一种误解，即疾控中心没有考虑过：如果实施封锁，会对经济或教育造成什么损害？

sentences.en: I wasn't there at the time, but I can tell you that in all of our recommendations, there is explicitly an understanding of the non-direct health-related costs,
sentences.zh: 我当时不在那里，但我可以告诉你，在我们所有的建议中，都明确包含了对非直接健康相关成本的理解，

sentences.en: whether that's of vaccinations or other recommendations.
sentences.zh: 无论是疫苗接种还是其他建议。

sentences.en: And it should be.
sentences.zh: 理应如此。

sentences.en: Now, CDC isn't always privy to what all of those things might be.
sentences.zh: 不过，疾控中心并不总是能获悉所有这些情况。

sentences.en: So to give you an example, during the Ebola epidemic, we wanted to track all incoming travelers, but they were coming into dozens of airports 24-7, and we had no way to do that.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，在埃博拉疫情期间，我们想追踪所有入境旅客，但他们24小时全天候从几十个机场入境，我们根本无法做到。

sentences.en: I didn't know, as CDC director, that the transportation department had the authority to mandate that all flights funnel into a limited number of airports.
sentences.zh: 作为疾控中心主任，我当时并不知道交通部有权强制要求所有航班集中到少数几个机场。

sentences.en: So instead of 32 airports, they could make it just five.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，他们可以将32个机场缩减为5个。

sentences.en: And with just five, we could figure out a way to track every incoming passenger from the affected countries.
sentences.zh: 只要有5个机场，我们就能想办法追踪每一位来自受影响国家的入境旅客。

sentences.en: So when you have a cross-government collaboration, you often identify new ways to do something more effectively or costs or benefits or potentials that you didn't know otherwise.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你进行跨政府合作时，你往往能发现更有效的新方法，或者发现原本不知道的成本、收益或潜力。

sentences.en: So there's been this ongoing debate about whether the president should have the freedom to fire heads of agencies within the executive branch for any reason.
sentences.zh: 关于总统是否应该有权以任何理由解雇行政部门下属机构的负责人，一直存在争议。

sentences.en: The CDC director can be fired for any reason.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心主任可以被以任何理由解雇。

sentences.en: And in fact, Susan Maneres was fired by the Trump administration this past August after only one month on the job.
sentences.zh: 事实上，苏珊·马内雷斯（Susan Maneres）在去年8月上任仅一个月后就被特朗普政府解雇了。

sentences.en: Do you think that's a good idea for the president to have that kind of latitude?
sentences.zh: 你认为总统拥有这种自由度是件好事吗？

sentences.en: And is there a better model for this?
sentences.zh: 有没有更好的模式？

sentences.en: The fact is, and this came up when just recently Congress made the CDC director position one that is Senate confirmed.
sentences.zh: 事实是，就在最近，国会将疾控中心主任职位改为需要参议院确认的职位时，这个问题就出现了。

sentences.en: There are pros and cons of that approach.
sentences.zh: 这种做法有利有弊。

sentences.en: But fundamentally, if you're a CDC director and the administration doesn't agree with you, you're not going to be able to get your job done.
sentences.zh: 但从根本上说，如果你是疾控中心主任，而政府不同意你的观点，你就无法完成工作。

sentences.en: So it doesn't really make sense to keep someone in if they're not part of the team.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一个人不是团队的一员，留任他确实没有意义。

sentences.en: That's different from a technical agency that may need to make non-political decisions on the economy or something else.
sentences.zh: 这与那些可能需要在经济或其他方面做出非政治性决策的技术机构不同。

sentences.en: But there's a related issue which has to do with what are called national statistical products.
sentences.zh: 但还有一个相关问题，涉及所谓的“国家统计产品”。

sentences.en: It sounds like a boring term, and it is a boring term, but it's actually...
sentences.zh: 听起来是个枯燥的术语，确实也很枯燥，但它实际上……

sentences.en: Please explain.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下。

sentences.en: It's quite an important term.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的术语。

sentences.en: There are certain publications or series that are considered so important that they be not politically tampered with,
sentences.zh: 有些出版物或系列被认为极其重要，必须免受政治干预，

sentences.en: that they have been national statistical products,
sentences.zh: 因此它们被定为国家统计产品，

sentences.en: including some of the publications from the National Center for Health Statistics, which is part of the CDC.
sentences.zh: 其中包括隶属于疾控中心的国家卫生统计中心发布的一些出版物。

sentences.en: It actually was independent for a while, then it became part of the CDC.
sentences.zh: 它曾经独立过一段时间，后来成为了疾控中心的一部分。

sentences.en: And as the CDC director, I was allowed to know what they were going to publish in terms of the title.
sentences.zh: 作为疾控中心主任，我有权知道他们要发布什么标题的内容。

sentences.en: Like, they're going to publish, not even the title, they're going to publish a publication on X.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们要发布关于X的出版物，甚至连标题都不能提前看。

sentences.en: But I was not permitted legally to see that report before the media saw that report.
sentences.zh: 但在法律上，我不被允许在媒体看到报告之前查看该报告。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: And that also goes for things like the Bureau of Labor Statistics employment data,
sentences.zh: 这也适用于劳工统计局的就业数据等内容，

sentences.en: because you really want people to have confidence in it.
sentences.zh: 因为你确实希望人们对这些数据有信心。

sentences.en: Now, in recent months, I learned, really to my astonishment,
sentences.zh: 最近几个月，我非常惊讶地了解到，

sentences.en: that that was not a legal or legislative protection.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一种法律或立法保护。

sentences.en: That was the result of a directive from OMB.
sentences.zh: 这只是管理与预算办公室（OMB）的一项指令的结果。

sentences.en: And if it can be established by OMB, it can be changed by OMB.
sentences.zh: 如果它是由管理与预算办公室确立的，那么它也可以由该办公室更改。

sentences.en: So I think it is really important for everyone that there is information that is produced by the experts in that information
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，对于每个人来说，由相关领域的专家生产信息，

sentences.en: with transparent methodology and hasn't been meddled with by a politician.
sentences.zh: 并采用透明的方法论，且不被政客干预，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: I think that's so important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这太重要了。

sentences.en: And one of the things that people may not realize is when an agency like the CDC is producing this kind of very important health data,
sentences.zh: 人们可能没有意识到的一点是，当像疾控中心这样的机构生产这种非常重要的健康数据时，

sentences.en: it's not just for public consumption at large.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是为了大众消费。

sentences.en: There's a whole network of researchers outside of the federal government that absolutely depend on this data,
sentences.zh: 联邦政府之外还有一个庞大的研究人员网络，他们绝对依赖这些数据，

sentences.en: can't create or collect it on their own.
sentences.zh: 他们自己无法创建或收集这些数据。

sentences.en: It's just too expensive to do.
sentences.zh: 因为成本太高了。

sentences.en: And so there's this vast infrastructure that really the CDC and other similar public health agencies are kind of upholding up from the bottom.
sentences.zh: 所以存在着一个庞大的基础设施，实际上是疾控中心和其他类似的公共卫生机构在底部支撑着它。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And this goes also for some of the survey systeMs.
sentences.zh: 这也适用于一些调查系统。

sentences.en: There are surveys that CDC does, and the results are anonymized, so you could never find who answered what.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心会进行一些调查，结果是匿名的，所以你永远无法查出是谁回答了什么。

sentences.en: But researchers, they're gold mines of information, and CDC will do the basic analyses of them and make them available for researchers to look at more.
sentences.zh: 但对于研究人员来说，这些是信息金矿，疾控中心会对其进行基础分析，并提供给研究人员进行更深入的研究。

sentences.en: And that's another essential function of CDC.
sentences.zh: 这也是疾控中心的另一个核心职能。

sentences.en: Getting back to your first question of why do we need a CDC, it establishes the standard for that,
sentences.zh: 回到你最初的问题，为什么我们需要疾控中心？因为它为这些工作建立了标准，

sentences.en: and then states figure out how to apply that.
sentences.zh: 然后各州再研究如何应用这些标准。

sentences.en: So if you had a magic wand, what would be at the top of your list for reforming the CDC?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你有一根魔杖，你改革疾控中心的首要任务是什么？

sentences.en: Well, CDC is undergoing attacks, political and even physical, that are unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 嗯，疾控中心正遭受着前所未有的政治甚至人身攻击。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We've had, for the first time, the firing of a CDC director.
sentences.zh: 我们第一次经历了疾控中心主任被解雇的情况。

sentences.en: About a quarter of CDC staff have either fired or resigned.
sentences.zh: 大约四分之一的疾控中心员工被解雇或辞职了。

sentences.en: Most of the leadership of the agency has left.
sentences.zh: 该机构的大部分领导层都已经离开。

sentences.en: You have, by last count, a dozen or 15 political appointees basically running the agency.
sentences.zh: 据最近统计，基本上有十几或十五名政治任命人员在管理该机构。

sentences.en: That has never happened before.
sentences.zh: 这种情况以前从未发生过。

sentences.en: You mentioned the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices.
sentences.zh: 你提到了免疫实践咨询委员会。

sentences.en: That's a committee that has used the highest standards of evidence and protection from conflicts of interest for decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，该委员会一直采用最高的证据标准，并防范利益冲突。

sentences.en: And it's been basically taken over by a group of people who have very limited knowledge of vaccines, most of them, not all of them,
sentences.zh: 但它基本上被一群对疫苗知之甚少的人接管了，他们中的大多数人，并非全部，

sentences.en: and who have made recommendations that are so at variance with basic medical concepts that the professional societies, doctors, nurses, and the insurers have said,
sentences.zh: 他们提出的建议与基本的医学概念大相径庭，以至于专业协会、医生、护士和保险公司都表示，

sentences.en: we're going to ignore what it says because it doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 我们要无视它的建议，因为它根本说不通。

sentences.en: So this is a very difficult time.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常困难的时期。

sentences.en: And I don't think we're going to go back to the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们能回到过去。

sentences.en: I think we're going to have to go forward to a CDC that's faster, that's better at communicating, that has better partnerships and alliances,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须向前看，建立一个更快速、沟通更顺畅、拥有更好伙伴关系和联盟的疾控中心，

sentences.en: and that delivers results that people can feel, that provides tangible benefits for people to understand and live a healthier, safer life.
sentences.zh: 一个能带来人们切实感受到的成果，提供有形利益，让人们理解并过上更健康、更安全生活的疾控中心。

sentences.en: I think one of the things that has to happen more is that CDC needs to be more tightly aligned with state and local governments.
sentences.zh: 我认为必须加强的一点是，疾控中心需要与州和地方政府更紧密地结合。

sentences.en: Because I had the benefit of joining CDC as director after having been New York City Health Commissioner.
sentences.zh: 因为我在担任纽约市卫生局局长之后才加入疾控中心担任主任，这让我受益匪浅。

sentences.en: So I had a pretty good sense of what was needed on the front lines.
sentences.zh: 所以我对一线需要什么有相当好的了解。

sentences.en: And I felt there was a little too much of a disconnect between folks at the CDC headquarters in Atlanta and folks out there on the front lines.
sentences.zh: 我感到亚特兰大疾控中心总部的人和一线的人之间存在一点脱节。

sentences.en: And this is not a political comment about this policy or that.
sentences.zh: 这不是针对某项政策的政治评论。

sentences.en: It's how fast you need results, how practical recommendations are.
sentences.zh: 而是关于你需要多快得到结果，以及建议有多实用。

sentences.en: And one of the things I did while I was there was I increased the number of CDC staff embedded in state and local health departments,
sentences.zh: 我在任期间所做的一件事就是增加了派驻到州和地方卫生部门的疾控中心员工数量，

sentences.en: especially early in their career.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那些职业生涯早期的员工。

sentences.en: So people could come in, spend a few years at a city or county or state health department, learn what it looks like on the front lines,
sentences.zh: 这样人们可以进来，在市、县或州卫生部门工作几年，了解一线的情况，

sentences.en: and then rotate to CDC where they would be able to provide more practical, helpful guidance.
sentences.zh: 然后再轮岗到疾控中心，这样他们就能提供更实用、更有帮助的指导。

sentences.en: The person who founded CDC, Joseph Mountain, wrote that he thought every CDC officer should have spent at least a year as a county health officer.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心的创始人约瑟夫·芒廷（Joseph Mountain）曾写道，他认为每位疾控中心官员都应该至少担任过一年的县卫生官员。

sentences.en: Long enough, he wrote, to have proposed a budget and gotten it through the city council.
sentences.zh: 他写道，时间要长到足以提出预算并使其在市议会获得通过。

sentences.en: Well, this brings up an interesting point that I'm interested in your personal biography.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这引出了一个我感兴趣的话题，关于你的个人履历。

sentences.en: I mean, the mayor of a city, the mayor of the city of New York, you know, has very different powers than the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 我是说，市长，纽约市的市长，你知道，其拥有的权力与美国总统非常不同。

sentences.en: There's also a big difference between, you know, what states and cities can legislate versus what the federal government can do.
sentences.zh: 州和城市可以立法的内容与联邦政府可以做的事情之间也存在巨大差异。

sentences.en: Still, you know, in terms of public health, you know, well, basically, what were you able to do as NYC?
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，在公共卫生方面，基本上，你在担任纽约市卫生局局长时能做的事情，有哪些是你在担任疾控中心主任时根本无法提出的？我想问的是这个问题。

sentences.en: Health Commissioner that you could never propose as the CDC director, I guess is the question I'm asking.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我告诉你，当我到达疾控中心时，我感到很震惊，因为疾控中心主任的权力比纽约市卫生局局长要小得多。

sentences.en: Well, I'll tell you, I found it a shock when I got to CDC because the CDC director is way, way, way less powerful than the New York City Health Commissioner.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为纽约市卫生局局长，我有大量灵活的资源可以投入到新兴的健康威胁或潜在的新项目中。

sentences.en: So, as New York City Health Commissioner, I had substantial flexible resources that I could devote to emerging health threats or potential new prograMs.
sentences.zh: 运作方式是，如果一个领域的钱没花完，我们可以把它花在另一个领域。

sentences.en: And the way that worked was if money weren't spent in one area, we could spend it in another area.
sentences.zh: 而且资金不可避免地会有剩余，所以你可以花掉它。

sentences.en: And inevitably, money gets underspent, and so you can spend it.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府传统上并不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: That's not how the federal government has traditionally worked.
sentences.zh: 如果你不按照国会分配的方式花钱，我们总是被告知你可能会坐牢，因为国会就是你的董事会。

sentences.en: If you don't spend the money in the way that Congress allocates it, we were always told you could go to jail because Congress is your board of directors.
sentences.zh: 这被称为违反《反亏空法》（Anti-Deficiency Act）。

sentences.en: And so that was called an Anti-Deficiency Act violation.
sentences.zh: 但随着这种关于扣留资金的新理论出现，目前的政府似乎并不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: But with this new theory on impoundment, that seems not to be the way the current administration is working.
sentences.zh: 但这确实意味着，作为纽约市卫生局局长，我拥有的灵活资金实际上比我担任疾控中心主任时多出20倍。

sentences.en: But that meant that I literally, I literally had 20 times more flexible dollars as New York City Health Commissioner that I had as CDC director.
sentences.zh: 第二个巨大的区别是，作为疾控中心主任，我对疾控中心的不同部门几乎没有控制权，因为大约有200个预算项目，

sentences.en: Second big difference was that as the CDC director, I had very little control over the different parts of CDC because there are something like 200 budget lines,
sentences.zh: 它们各自运行自己的项目、部门和中心。

sentences.en: and they all run their own programs, divisions, and centers.
sentences.zh: 主任充其量就像是指挥管弦乐队，但更现实的情况是，更像是走在旁边陪衬。

sentences.en: And the director is kind of, you know, at best conducting an orchestra, but more realistically kind of walking alongside.
sentences.zh: 所以当我想启动一个将数百名员工派往州和地方卫生部门的新项目时，我根本没有办法做到。

sentences.en: So when I wanted to start a new program of putting hundreds of staff into state and local health departments, I had no way to do that.
sentences.zh: 我不得不低声下气地去求我的中心和部门主管，说，你们能支持三四个吗？

sentences.en: I had to go kind of cup in hand to my center and division director and said, would you support three or four?
sentences.zh: 你们能支持五六个吗？

sentences.en: Would you support five or six?
sentences.zh: 另一个非常不同的地方实际上是权力。

sentences.en: The other thing that was so very different was actually authority.
sentences.zh: 作为纽约市卫生局局长，我拥有很大的权力。

sentences.en: So as New York City Health Commissioner, I had a lot of authority.
sentences.zh: 比如当我担任助理局长并负责结核病控制项目时，我们对拘留法进行了现代化改造。

sentences.en: Like when I was assistant commissioner and I ran the tuberculosis control program, we modernized the detention laws.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你患有结核病但不吃药，我们可以下令将你拘留在医院直到治愈。

sentences.en: So if you had tuberculosis and you didn't take your medicines, we could order you detained in a hospital until you were cured.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果一家餐馆在不卫生的条件下供应食物，我们可以关闭它。

sentences.en: And, you know, if a restaurant is serving food in unsanitary conditions, we could close it.
sentences.zh: 如果某个地方存在环境危害，我们可以下令消除它。

sentences.en: If there is an environmental hazard in a place, we could order it to be abated.
sentences.zh: 所以作为城市卫生局局长，尤其是纽约市的局长，拥有巨大的权力和权威，因为这座城市介于州和城市之间。

sentences.en: So there was a huge amount more of authority and power as a city health commissioner, especially New York City, because the city is kind of a hybrid between a state and a city.
sentences.zh: 纽约州下放给了纽约市许多大多数城市没有权力做的事情。

sentences.en: The New York State has delegated to New York City a lot of things that most cities don't have the authority to do.
sentences.zh: 它有自己的卫生法规。

sentences.en: It has its own health code.
sentences.zh: 它有自己的卫生委员会。

sentences.en: It has its own board of health.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以说，从纽约市来到疾控中心，特别是考虑到迈克·布隆伯格（Mike Bloomberg），他有一所以他名字命名的公共卫生学院，并且愿意在公共卫生方面投入，

sentences.en: So I can say that coming from New York City, particularly with Mike Bloomberg, who has a public health school named after him and was willing to do public health stuff to the CDC,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人沮丧的转变，因为尽管组织规模更大，但权力和权威却少得多。

sentences.en: it was a very frustrating transition because the amount of authority and power was so much less, even though the organization is larger.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人沮丧的转变，因为尽管组织规模更大，但权力和权威却少得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, would you like to see that power sort of – if there was a U.S.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我是说，你是否希望看到那种权力——如果美国有一个

sentences.en: health commissioner, would that be a better system?
sentences.zh: 卫生专员，那会是一个更好的体制吗？

sentences.en: I don't think that will ever happen.
sentences.zh: 我认为那永远不会发生。

sentences.en: And we do have a very decentralized federal system in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且美国确实有一个非常分散的联邦体制，

sentences.en: where we decentralize the states.
sentences.zh: 我们将权力下放给了各州。

sentences.en: It's what I think would be more effective is a system where there's more alignment between city, county, state, and federal, so that not that everyone's working in lockstep,
sentences.zh: 我认为更有效的体制是城市、县、州和联邦之间有更多协同的体制，并不是说每个人都要步调一致，

sentences.en: but if we're going to try to address the opiate overdose problem or reduce food poisoning or reduce strokes or heart attacks or cancers,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们打算解决阿片类药物过量问题，或者减少食物中毒、中风、心脏病或癌症，

sentences.en: we can say, all right, let's do this in a coordinated way that's learned from each other, maybe we'll try three different approaches and compare them.
sentences.zh: 我们可以说，好吧，让我们以协调一致的方式来做，互相学习，也许我们可以尝试三种不同的方法并进行比较。

sentences.en: Right now, there's just too much distance between the different parts of the public health system.
sentences.zh: 目前，公共卫生系统各部门之间的距离太远了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I want to end smoking in restaurants and bars, but then we decide, oh, this is much better.
sentences.zh: 我想在餐馆和酒吧禁烟，但后来我们决定，哦，这好多了。

sentences.en: I can breathe.
sentences.zh: 我可以呼吸了。

sentences.en: So that's, I think, the real challenge for public health in a democracy.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这是民主制度下公共卫生面临的真正挑战。

sentences.en: I tell in the book two stories from the Bloomberg administration.
sentences.zh: 我在书中讲了两个关于彭博政府的故事。

sentences.en: When Mayor Bloomberg was running for re-election for the first time, I was really enthusiastic about his leadership because he was an excellent manager.
sentences.zh: 当彭博市长第一次竞选连任时，我对他非常热衷，因为他是一位出色的管理者。

sentences.en: He was really focused on public health.
sentences.zh: 他非常关注公共卫生。

sentences.en: We had made a lot of progress.
sentences.zh: 我们取得了很大进展。

sentences.en: We had banned smoking in bars.
sentences.zh: 我们禁止了在酒吧吸烟。

sentences.en: We had raised tobacco tax.
sentences.zh: 我们提高了烟草税。

sentences.en: We had done new things on HIV care and prevention.
sentences.zh: 我们在艾滋病护理和预防方面做了新的尝试。

sentences.en: And so I asked one of his inner circle, how can I help with his re-election?
sentences.zh: 所以我问他核心圈子里的一个人，我该如何为他的连任提供帮助？

sentences.en: And she said, I'll tell you how you can help.
sentences.zh: 她说，我告诉你你怎么帮。

sentences.en: Let us put you in a closet and put duct tape over your mouth until after the election.
sentences.zh: 让我们把你关进壁橱，用胶带封住你的嘴，直到选举结束。

sentences.en: And after he won re-election, he called all of the commissioners together and he said,
sentences.zh: 在他赢得连任后，他召集了所有的专员，他说，

sentences.en: you know, look, I financed my own election, so I don't owe anything to anyone.
sentences.zh: 你们知道，看，我自己出资竞选，所以我不需要亏欠任何人。

sentences.en: And our job is to do the hard stuff that nobody else is going to do, like building the new water tunnel for New York City,
sentences.zh: 我们的工作就是做那些没人愿意做的困难事情，比如为纽约市修建新的输水隧道，

sentences.en: a multi-billion dollar effort that would take many, many years and he would never get the credit for.
sentences.zh: 这是一个耗资数十亿美元、需要花费很多很多年，而且他永远不会因此获得赞誉的工程。

sentences.en: And so Mayor Bloomberg said, it's kind of a mark that we're not doing our job, that my approval rating is, you know, in the mid-70s.
sentences.zh: 所以彭博市长说，我的支持率在75%左右，这反而说明我们没有做好自己的工作。

sentences.en: And if we do our job, the approval rating will come down.
sentences.zh: 如果我们做好了工作，支持率就会下降。

sentences.en: And the head of his communications unit shouted from the back of the room, we're counting on you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他的通讯部门负责人从房间后面大喊：我们指望你了，汤姆。

sentences.en: So, yes, it can be unpopular.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这可能会不受欢迎。

sentences.en: But I will say, when we made all restaurants and bars smoke-free, it was a huge fight, a huge fight.
sentences.zh: 但我得说，当我们让所有餐馆和酒吧禁烟时，那是一场巨大的斗争，非常激烈的斗争。

sentences.en: And, you know, the tabloids had a field day, criticizing the mayor and me and everybody else.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，小报们在那段时间大肆炒作，批评市长、我和其他所有人。

sentences.en: And by first or second year after, people really appreciated it.
sentences.zh: 但在那之后的第一年或第二年，人们真的很感激它。

sentences.en: And the opposite, people said, oh, people are going to not go to bars and restaurants.
sentences.zh: 而且相反的情况是，人们说，哦，人们将不会去酒吧和餐馆了。

sentences.en: The opposite happened.
sentences.zh: 结果恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Oh, they're so much more pleasant.
sentences.zh: 哦，它们变得舒适多了。

sentences.en: We'll go there, we'll eat, we'll hang out for longer.
sentences.zh: 我们会去那里，吃饭，待更长的时间。

sentences.en: And I think this is the case with many public health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多公共卫生问题都是如此。

sentences.en: Another example of this, and it's important to see the kind of evolution of social change I discuss in the book,
sentences.zh: 另一个例子，重要的是要看到我在书中讨论的那种社会变革的演变，

sentences.en: is think of a generation or two when it was normal for a family to load up the car, drive to a beach, not wearing seatbelts, put on not sunblock, but tanning lotion.
sentences.zh: 想想一两代人之前，家庭装满车、开车去海滩、不系安全带、涂抹的不是防晒霜而是美黑乳液，这都是很正常的。

sentences.en: Have a few beers, hop back into their car without putting on seatbelts, drive to a restaurant, smoke in the restaurant, have a few more drinks, and then,
sentences.zh: 喝几杯啤酒，不系安全带跳回车里，开车去餐馆，在餐馆里抽烟，再喝几杯，然后，

sentences.en: not wearing seatbelts again, drive home.
sentences.zh: 再次不系安全带，开车回家。

sentences.en: I think you might have been spying on my family.
sentences.zh: 我想你可能一直在监视我的家人。

sentences.en: Well, most families, because that was the social norm.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大多数家庭都是这样，因为那是当时的社会规范。

sentences.en: That was the social norm.
sentences.zh: 那是当时的社会规范。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there's still too much driving under the influence, there's still too much skin cancer, there's still too much exposure to secondhand smoke,
sentences.zh: 现在仍然有太多的酒驾，仍然有太多的皮肤癌，仍然有太多的二手烟暴露，

sentences.en: but those things are much less common, and they're no longer the social norm.
sentences.zh: 但这些事情已经少见多了，它们不再是社会规范。

sentences.en: And that's the reflection of huge progress, progress that has saved millions of lives.
sentences.zh: 这是巨大进步的体现，这种进步挽救了数百万人的生命。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: It's also a social norm to not die of measles and not be in an iron lung, and that has happened for enough decades that people probably, you know,
sentences.zh: 不因麻疹而死、不躺在铁肺里也是一种社会规范，这种情况已经持续了几十年，以至于人们可能，你知道，

sentences.en: like they're playing footsie with risk that they probably don't understand.
sentences.zh: 就像他们在玩弄风险，而他们可能并不理解。

sentences.en: How do you make them understand that?
sentences.zh: 你如何让他们理解这一点？

sentences.en: I think this has been a real challenge.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: First off, there have been anti-vaccination movements ever since the first vaccines.
sentences.zh: 首先，自第一种疫苗问世以来，就一直存在反疫苗运动。

sentences.en: And in the book, I talk about Ben Franklin, whose four-year-old child died from smallpox, and there was misinformation that he had died from the vaccine,
sentences.zh: 在书中，我谈到了本·富兰克林，他四岁的孩子死于天花，当时有错误信息称孩子死于疫苗，

sentences.en: and Franklin got on the social media of his day, which was his gazette that he was putting out, to say, no, the child died from the virus itself.
sentences.zh: 富兰克林在他那个时代的社交媒体上，也就是他发行的公报上说，不，孩子是死于病毒本身。

sentences.en: And even a half a century later, when he wrote his autobiography, he very movingly went back to that episode, and he said, you know, basically,
sentences.zh: 即使在半个世纪后，当他写自传时，他非常感人地回顾了那段插曲，他说，你知道，基本上，

sentences.en: put yourself in the position of a parent whose child has died.
sentences.zh: 把自己放在一个孩子去世的父母的位置上。

sentences.en: Wouldn't you have rather done everything possible to prevent it?
sentences.zh: 难道你不想尽一切可能去预防它吗？

sentences.en: So there are effective ways to find the messaging.
sentences.zh: 所以有有效的方法来传达信息。

sentences.en: We also find that vaccines are victims of their own success.
sentences.zh: 我们还发现疫苗是其自身成功的受害者。

sentences.en: We don't have any problems getting people in Africa to get vaccinated against meningitis, because it's a terrible disease, and they see people with terrible meningitis.
sentences.zh: 我们在非洲让人们接种脑膜炎疫苗没有任何问题，因为这是一种可怕的疾病，他们亲眼见过患有严重脑膜炎的人。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I want that vaccine.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我想要那种疫苗。

sentences.en: This means that we need to improve communication.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们需要改善沟通。

sentences.en: We need to listen carefully to people's concerns.
sentences.zh: 我们需要仔细倾听人们的担忧。

sentences.en: We need to provide objective data.
sentences.zh: 我们需要提供客观的数据。

sentences.en: Fortunately, although some of the myths and the falsehoods get a lot of coverage,
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，尽管一些神话和谎言得到了很多报道，

sentences.en: still the vast majority of Americans understand that vaccines are life-saving and get their kids vaccinated on schedule.
sentences.zh: 但绝大多数美国人仍然明白疫苗可以挽救生命，并按计划让他们的孩子接种疫苗。

sentences.en: But that's not an assured progress.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一种有保障的进步。

sentences.en: We're seeing this fire hose of falsehoods about vaccines.
sentences.zh: 我们正在看到关于疫苗的谎言如洪水般涌来。

sentences.en: And it means that our defenses against microbial killers are going to get weaker.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们对抗微生物杀手的防御能力将会减弱。
